messages.content: How can one install the `s3cmd` command-line tool on various Linux distributions?
To install `s3cmd` on Linux, use `sudo yum install s3cmd` for RHEL or CentOS distributions, or `sudo apt install s3cmd` for Debian or Ubuntu distributions.
What are the essential steps and specific values required to configure `s3cmd` for use with Arbutus object storage?

To configure `s3cmd` for Arbutus object storage, execute `s3cmd --configure`. During the configuration process, you'll need to input your Access Key and Secret Key. Crucially, set both the 'S3 Endpoint' and the 'DNS-style bucket+hostname:port template' to `object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca`, and select 'Yes' when prompted to 'Use HTTPS protocol'.
How do you create a new bucket in Arbutus object storage using `s3cmd`, and what are the naming conventions for buckets?

To create a new bucket, use the command `s3cmd mb s3://BUCKET_NAME/`, replacing `BUCKET_NAME` with your desired name. Bucket names must be unique across the entire Arbutus object storage solution and can only consist of upper-case letters (A-Z), lower-case letters (a-z), digits (0-9), periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores (_).
How do you upload a file to an Arbutus object storage bucket using the `s3cmd` tool?

To upload a file to an Arbutus object storage bucket, use the `s3cmd put` command. For example, `$ s3cmd put --guess-mime-type FILE_NAME.dat s3://BUCKET_NAME/FILE_NAME.dat`. The `--guess-mime-type` parameter helps in automatically determining the file's Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (MIME) type based on its extension, otherwise it defaults to `binary/octet-stream`.
What `s3cmd` command is used to delete a specific file from an Arbutus object storage bucket?

To delete a specific file from an Arbutus object storage bucket, use the `s3cmd rm` command. The syntax is `$ s3cmd rm s3://BUCKET_NAME/FILE_NAME.dat`, where you specify the bucket name and the exact file to be deleted.
How can you make an Arbutus object storage bucket and all its contents publicly accessible using `s3cmd`?

To make an Arbutus object storage bucket and recursively all its files publicly accessible, use the `s3cmd setacl --acl-public -r s3://BUCKET_NAME/` command. After this, files within the bucket can be accessed via URLs such as `https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca/PROJECT_ID:BUCKET_NAME/FILE_NAME.dat`.
How can I check the status of an Arbutus object storage bucket using the `s3cmd` tool?

To check the status of an Arbutus object storage bucket with the `s3cmd` tool, you can use the command `s3cmd info s3://BUCKET_NAME/`, where `BUCKET_NAME` should be replaced with the actual name of your bucket.
What kind of information is provided in the output when I check the status of an Arbutus object storage bucket using `s3cmd info`?

When you use the `s3cmd info` command, the output provides details such as the bucket's location, payer, expiration rules, policies, CORS settings, Access Control Lists (ACLs) for anonymous and user access, and the bucket's URL.
What is the main purpose of the document regarding Arbutus object storage?
The document provides instructions on how to set up and access Arbutus object storage using s3cmd, which is one of the available object storage clients for this type of storage.
How can a user install the `s3cmd` command on a Linux distribution to access Arbutus object storage?
The `s3cmd` command can be installed using `sudo yum install s3cmd` for RHEL/CentOS distributions or `sudo apt install s3cmd` for Debian/Ubuntu distributions.
What command is used to initiate the configuration process for the `s3cmd` tool when setting up Arbutus object storage?
The command `s3cmd --configure` is used to configure the `s3cmd` tool.
What key identifiers are required during the `s3cmd` configuration for Arbutus object storage?
The Access Key and Secret Key are required identifiers, which can be provided or created using the `openstack ec2 credentials create` command.
What S3 Endpoint should be specified when configuring `s3cmd` for Arbutus object storage?
The S3 Endpoint `object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca` should be specified.
What value should be entered for the DNS-style bucket+hostname:port template during `s3cmd` configuration for Arbutus object storage?
The value `object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca` should be entered for the DNS-style bucket+hostname:port template.
Is it recommended to use HTTPS protocol when configuring `s3cmd` for Arbutus object storage, and what is its benefit?
Yes, it is recommended to use HTTPS protocol. It protects all communication with Amazon S3 servers from third-party eavesdropping.
What command is used to create a new bucket in Arbutus object storage using `s3cmd`?
The command `s3cmd mb s3://BUCKET_NAME/` is used to create a new bucket.
What are the naming conventions for buckets in the Arbutus object storage solution?
Bucket names must be unique across the Arbutus object storage solution and can only use upper-case letters, lower-case letters, digits, periods, hyphens, and underscores (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, ., -, and _).
How can a user view the status and information of a bucket in Arbutus object storage using `s3cmd`?
The `s3cmd info s3://BUCKET_NAME/` command can be used to see the status of a bucket.
What `s3cmd` command is used to upload a file to a bucket in Arbutus object storage?
To upload a file, use the command `s3cmd put --guess-mime-type FILE_NAME.dat s3://BUCKET_NAME/FILE_NAME.dat`, specifying the bucket and file names.
How can a user delete a file from a bucket in Arbutus object storage using `s3cmd`?
The command `s3cmd rm s3://BUCKET_NAME/FILE_NAME.dat` is used to delete a file from a bucket.
What `s3cmd` command makes a bucket and all its contents publicly accessible in Arbutus object storage?
The command `s3cmd setacl --acl-public -r s3://BUCKET_NAME/` makes a bucket and recursively every file in it publicly accessible.
What is the format of a URL for accessing publicly available files in an Arbutus object storage bucket?
Publicly accessible files can be accessed via URLs in the format `https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca/PROJECT_ID:BUCKET_NAME/FILE_NAME.dat`.
How can a user limit access to a bucket in Arbutus object storage to only the owner using `s3cmd`?
The command `s3cmd setacl --acl-private s3://BUCKET_NAME/` can be used to limit access to the bucket to only the owner.
Where can users find more sophisticated examples for managing bucket policies for their Arbutus Object Store?
More sophisticated examples for managing bucket policies, including those using s3cmd, are available on the main Arbutus object storage page.
What is the primary purpose of the instructions provided on this page?
This page provides instructions on how to set up and access Arbutus object storage using WinSCP, which is one of the object storage clients available for this storage type.
What are the initial configuration settings required in WinSCP to connect to Arbutus object storage?

When configuring a "New Session" in WinSCP for Arbutus object storage, you must set the "File protocol" to Amazon S3, the "Host name" to `object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca`, the "Port number" to 443, and the "Access key ID" to your unique `20_DIGIT_ACCESS_KEY`.
What crucial advanced setting must be changed in WinSCP for it to correctly work with Arbutus object storage, and why is it important?

It is crucial to change the "URL style:" setting from "Virtual Host" to "Path." This setting is found by navigating through "Edit" > "Advanced..." > "Environment" > "S3" > "Protocol options." This change is vital because without it, WinSCP will not function and will display hostname resolution errors.
What is the main purpose of the instructions provided on this page regarding Arbutus object storage?
The instructions on this page explain how to set up and access Arbutus object storage using WinSCP.
What is WinSCP in the context of accessing Arbutus object storage?
WinSCP is one of the object storage clients available for accessing Arbutus object storage.
Where can users install the WinSCP client for accessing Arbutus object storage?
Users can install the WinSCP client from https://winscp.net/.
What file protocol should be selected when configuring a new session in WinSCP for Arbutus object storage?
The 'Amazon S3' file protocol should be selected.
What hostname is required for configuring WinSCP to access Arbutus object storage?
The required hostname is object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca.
Which port number should be used in WinSCP settings when connecting to Arbutus object storage?
Port number 443 should be used.
What information is needed for the 'Access key ID' field during WinSCP configuration for Arbutus object storage?
A 20-digit access key ID is required.
What specific URL style setting must be changed in WinSCP's advanced configuration for Arbutus object storage, and what should it be changed to?
The 'URL style:' setting under 'Environment' > 'S3' > 'Protocol options' must be changed from 'Virtual Host' to 'Path'.
Why is it crucial to set the 'URL style' to 'Path' in WinSCP's advanced configuration for Arbutus object storage?
This 'Path' setting is important because otherwise WinSCP will not work and users will encounter hostname resolution errors.
After configuring WinSCP, what is the next step to begin using it for Arbutus object storage?
Users should click on the 'Login' button.
What common file management tasks can users perform using the WinSCP graphical user interface for Arbutus object storage?
Users can use the WinSCP GUI to create buckets and to transfer files.
How can users set Access Control Lists (ACLs) for files within WinSCP when connected to Arbutus object storage?
Right-clicking on a file in WinSCP allows users to set its ACL.
What is the primary purpose of using the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) with Arbutus object storage?

The AWS CLI provides instructions on how to set up and access Arbutus object storage, serving as one of the available object storage clients for this type of storage. It offers better support for large files (over 5GB) and includes a helpful `sync` command.
How do you install the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) to access Arbutus object storage?
You can install the AWS CLI, along with the required endpoint plugin, by running the following command: `pip install awscli awscli-plugin-endpoint`.
What are the essential steps for configuring the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) to work with Arbutus object storage?

To configure the AWS CLI, you first need to generate an access key ID and secret key using `openstack ec2 credentials create`. Next, you must edit or create the `~/.aws/credentials` file to add these generated keys. Finally, you need to edit the `~/.aws/config` file to add the endpoint plugin and specify the s3 and s3api endpoint URLs as `https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca` with `signature_version = s3v4`.
What is the primary purpose of the instructions provided for Arbutus object storage?
The instructions detail how to set up and access Arbutus object storage using the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI).
What role does the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) play with Arbutus object storage?
The AWS CLI is one of the available object storage clients for Arbutus object storage.
What are the main advantages of using the AWS CLI for Arbutus object storage compared to other clients?
The AWS CLI offers better support for large files (over 5 GB) and includes a helpful `sync` command.
Are all features of the AWS CLI fully tested when used with Arbutus object storage?
No, not all features of the AWS CLI have been tested with Arbutus object storage.
How do users install the AWS CLI and its necessary plugin for Arbutus object storage?
Users can install it by running the command `pip install awscli awscli-plugin-endpoint`.
What is the initial step to configure the AWS CLI for accessing Arbutus object storage credentials?
The first step is to generate an access key ID and secret key using the command `openstack ec2 credentials create`.
Where should the generated AWS access key ID and secret key be saved for AWS CLI configuration?
The generated `aws_access_key_id` and `aws_secret_access_key` should be added to the `~/.aws/credentials` file under the `[default]` section.
What specific configurations are required in the `~/.aws/config` file to connect the AWS CLI to Arbutus object storage?

The `~/.aws/config` file needs to specify the `endpoint` plugin, and set `endpoint_url = https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca` and `signature_version = s3v4` under the `[profile default]` section for both `s3` and `s3api`.
What environment variable should be set before running AWS CLI commands for Arbutus object storage?
The `AWS_PROFILE` environment variable should be set to `default` by executing `export AWS_PROFILE=default`.
What is the command to list containers using the AWS CLI for Arbutus object storage?
To list containers, the command `aws s3 ls <container-name>` is used.
How can a user synchronize a local directory to an Arbutus object storage container using the AWS CLI?
A user can synchronize a local directory using the command `aws s3 sync local_directory s3://container-name/prefix`.
Where can users find more examples for utilizing the AWS CLI with Arbutus object storage?
More examples can be found on an external site: https://docs.ovh.com/us/en/storage/getting_started_with_the_swift_S3_API/.
Why is it necessary to migrate virtual machine (VM) instances from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud, and what is the deadline for this migration?

Migration is required because the legacy Arbutus Cloud will be decommissioned in 2026. The specific deadline for both RAS and RAC projects to migrate their resources to the new Arbutus Cloud is August 31, 2026.
What are the key planning considerations users should address before migrating their cloud resources from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud?

Users should identify which resources require migration (versus deletion), whether instances are ephemeral or volume-backed, if any volumes exceed 150 GB (as they should be migrated using Globus), if automated deployment systems were used, and if custom DNS entries need updating due to new floating IP address ranges. They should also consider whether to use the OpenStack dashboard or CLI, confirm all users have active Alliance accounts, plan for potential service outages, and submit a migration request if their resources were obtained via the rapid access service.
What is the most important preparatory step before starting a migration from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud, and who bears responsibility for this step?

The most important preparatory step is to back up any critical data. Project owners are responsible for creating these backups, as the Arbutus Cloud teams do not provide backups or copies of instances.
What happens to bucket ACLs and user/project UUIDs when migrating object storage to the new Arbutus Cloud?

When migrating object storage to the new Arbutus Cloud, bucket ACLs (Access Control Lists) typically need to be recreated because most migration tools do not preserve them. Additionally, any user or project UUIDs referenced will be different in the new Arbutus Cloud.
How does object storage in the new Arbutus Cloud handle bucket names and unauthenticated public access?

In the new Arbutus Cloud, object storage uses tenants, meaning bucket name collisions are confined to individual projects. For public access to buckets without authentication, the tenant must be explicitly specified in the URL. The Tenant ID is identical to the OpenStack Project ID, and the URL for unauthenticated S3 access follows the format `https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca/<tenant-id>:<bucket-name>/<object-name>`.
What tool is recommended for migrating object storage to the new Arbutus Cloud, and what is its main limitation?

The document recommends rclone for migrating object storage to the new Arbutus Cloud. Its main limitation is that rclone will not copy bucket ACLs, so all access to the migrated buckets will initially default to private in the new location.
How can one confirm access to projects in both the legacy and new Arbutus Clouds after configuring OpenStack RC files?

To confirm access, activate an RC file in a shell session by sourcing it (e.g., `source opensrc.sh`). Then, test the configuration by running the command `openstack volume list`. It's important to remember that only one RC file can be active in a given shell session at a time.
What are the steps to migrate SSH key pairs from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud using the Horizon dashboard?

First, from the legacy Arbutus Horizon dashboard, navigate to 'Compute -> Key Pairs', click on the name of the key pair you wish to migrate, and copy its public key value. Next, on the new Arbutus Horizon dashboard, go to 'Compute -> Key Pairs', click on 'Import Public Key', provide a name for your key pair, and paste the copied public key. Repeat these steps for all necessary keys. Alternatively, SSH key pairs can also be generated or imported using the OpenStack Command Line Interface (CLI) with the command `openstack keypair create --public-key <public-keyfile> <name>`.
How does one migrate security groups and their associated rules from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud?

To migrate security groups, first go to 'Network -> Security Groups' on the legacy Arbutus Cloud and note all existing security groups and their rules. Then, on the new Arbutus Cloud, navigate to 'Network -> Security Groups' and re-create these security groups and their associated rules as needed. It is critical not to delete any default Egress security rules for IPv4 and IPv6, as removing them can lead to instances failing to retrieve configuration data. Security groups and rules can also be created via the CLI, for instance, using `openstack security group create <group-name>` and `openstack security group rule create --proto tcp --remote-ip 0.0.0.0/0 --dst-port 80 <group-name>`.
What specific modifications are required for the RC file downloaded from the new Arbutus Cloud to ensure proper authentication?

To modify the RC file from the new Arbutus cloud, you must add the lines `export OS_AUTH_TYPE=v3websso`, `export OS_IDENTITY_PROVIDER=atmosphere`, `export OS_PROTOCOL=openid`, and `export OS_PROJECT_DOMAIN_NAME=default`. Additionally, you must remove the lines containing `export OS_USER_DOMAIN_NAME="atmosphere" if [ -z "$OS_USER_DOMAIN_NAME" ]; then unset OS_USER_DOMAIN_NAME; fi` and `echo "Please enter your OpenStack Password for project $OS_PROJECT_NAME as user $OS_USERNAME: " read -sr OS_PASSWORD_INPUT export OS_PASSWORD=$OS_PASSWORD_INPUT`.
After modifying the RC file for the new Arbutus Cloud, what steps are necessary to set up the environment for using the OpenStack Client and other packages?

After modifying the RC file, you need to create a virtual environment by running `$ python3 -m venv openstack`, then activate it with `$ source openstack/bin/activate`, and finally install the necessary packages using `$ pip install python-openstackclient keystoneauth-websso python-manilaclient`.
What are the three main migration scenarios to consider when planning a migration to the new Arbutus Cloud?
The three general migration scenarios to consider are manual or orchestrated migration, migrating volume-backed instances, and migrating ephemeral instances.
What is the recommended size limit for volumes when migrating volume-backed instances between the legacy and new Arbutus Clouds using Glance images?
The migration method using Glance images is recommended for volumes less than 150GB in size. For volumes larger than that, the manual or orchestrated migration approach is preferred.
What are the initial steps in the legacy Arbutus Cloud web user interface for creating an image from a volume during the migration of a volume-backed instance?

First, shut down the instance and detach the volume. If the volume is for booting an instance, delete the instance but keep the volume. Then, navigate to 'Volumes -> Volumes' and select 'Upload to Image' from the drop-down menu, making sure to select RAW as the disk format.
How can one create a new image from an existing volume on the legacy Arbutus Cloud using the command line interface during a volume-backed instance migration?

You can create an image from a volume using the command line with `openstack image create --volume <volume name/id> <newimagename> --private`. This command runs in the background, and once the image is created, its status will eventually change from 'saving' to 'active' under 'Compute -> Images'.
What is the purpose of the `dd` utility when migrating volume-backed instances in the Arbutus Cloud?

The `dd` utility is used to create an image from a disk or volume. This image can then be uploaded to the new Arbutus Cloud and used to launch new instances, effectively making an identical copy of a volume from the legacy cloud on the new cloud.
When is the `dd` command recommended for migrating large volumes to the new Arbutus Cloud?

The `dd` command is recommended for migrating large volumes when image-based methods are not suitable, and when copying data using tools like `rsync` is not possible (e.g., for bootable volumes). It creates an identical copy of the volume on the new cloud.
How do you create an image from an attached volume on a temporary migration host using the `dd` utility and OpenStack CLI for Arbutus Cloud migration?

To create an image, first, ensure the volume is attached to the temporary migration host (e.g., as `/dev/vdb`). Then, execute the command: `dd if=/dev/vdb | openstack image create --private --container-format bare --disk-format raw "volumemigrate"`. Replace `/dev/vdb` with the actual device and `"volumemigrate"` with your desired image name.
What is the process for migrating large volumes from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud using the Linux 'dd' command?

To migrate large volumes using the `dd` command, first back up any important data. Next, create temporary instances (p1-1.5gb) on both the legacy and new clouds, and assign them floating IPs for SSH access. On the temporary legacy instance, install `epel-release`, `pv`, and `screen` packages. On the temporary new instance, run `chmod u+s /bin/dd`. Copy your SSH private key to the temporary legacy instance and ensure SSH security rules permit connections between the instances. For each volume to be moved, create an empty volume of the same size on the new cloud (marking it bootable if needed) and attach it to the new temporary instance. Attach the legacy volume you wish to copy to the temporary legacy instance. Finally, on the temporary legacy instance, execute a command similar to `sudo dd bs=16M if=/dev/vdb | pv -s 96G | ssh -i key.pem user@xxx.xx.xx.xx "sudo dd bs=16M of=/dev/vdb"` within a `screen` session to maintain connection. Once complete, an exact copy of the volume will be available on the new cloud.
When is Globus recommended for copying data between instances in the legacy and new Arbutus Clouds, and what are the initial steps to set it up?

Globus is recommended for copying very large data volumes, specifically those greater than 5TB, between instances in the legacy and new Arbutus Clouds. The initial setup involves requesting a Globus Connect Personal Plus subscription by emailing `globus@tech.alliancecan.ca`. After receiving and following the invitation, you must enable Globus Connect Personal on each cloud instance involved in the transfer. This includes installing the client, ensuring each VM has an external IP address, configuring firewall rules to permit communication on necessary ports, ensuring the user running Globus Connect Personal has data access, and running the client as a background process. Finally, as a Globus Connect Personal Plus subscriber, you create a shared endpoint on one or both virtual machines.
When should Globus be used for transferring data between cloud instances?
Globus is recommended for transferring very large data volumes, specifically those greater than 5TB, between cloud instances.
What is the recommended method for transferring small data volumes between cloud instances, and how does it generally work?

For small data volumes, rsync over SSH is recommended due to its good transfer speeds and incremental capabilities. The process generally involves SSHing to the legacy instance, executing an rsync command (e.g., `rsync -avzP -e 'ssh -i ~/.ssh/key.pem' /local/path/ remoteuser@remotehost:/path/to/files/`), and then verifying the data. Utilizing the IPv6 GUA network in OpenStack is also suggested for potentially improved data transfer performance.
What post-transfer configurations might be necessary after migrating data to a new instance?

After data is transferred to a new instance, several post-transfer configurations might be necessary, including updating host-based firewall rules, modifying DNS entries for custom domains, updating IP addresses in various configuration files (e.g., `/etc/hosts`, `/etc/resolv.conf`), altering usernames in database systems like MySQL, and renewing TLS certificates. It is essential to test the configuration thoroughly before informing the research team and users about the completion of the migration.
What post-transfer configuration activities might be necessary after migrating data to a new instance on the Arbutus Cloud?

After data is transferred, you may need to update firewall rules for new IP addresses, work with your DNS provider to update DNS entries for custom domains, update IP addresses in configuration files (e.g., /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf), alter usernames in databases like MySQL, and renew Let’s Encrypt TLS certificates.
What is the recommended procedure for migrating data between a legacy CephFS shared filesystem and a new CephFS shared filesystem on the Arbutus Cloud?

The recommended procedure is to first create an equivalent share in the new cloud for each legacy share. Then, mount both the legacy and new shares to separate locations on the same virtual machine in the new Arbutus Cloud. Finally, use a data copy tool like rsync to transfer the data from the old share to the new share.
What are the essential differences when creating and managing CephFS shares in the new Arbutus Cloud environment?

When creating and managing CephFS shares in the new Arbutus Cloud, you must create the new share and access keys using the new cloud web user interface. You also need to create a separate `ceph.conf` file, such as `ceph-new.conf`, and update the `mon_host` configuration value within this new file.
How should users transfer data between legacy and new CephFS shares during migration?

Users should mount both the legacy and new CephFS shares to separate locations on the same virtual machine in the new Arbutus Cloud. Then, use the `rsync` command with the `a`, `v`, and `P` flags to transfer data, for example: `rsync -avp /mnt/old-share/ /mnt/new-share/`. For long transfers, tools like `screen` or `tmux` are recommended to maintain the session.
What is the primary characteristic of object storage on the new Arbutus Cloud regarding migration?

Object storage on the new Arbutus Cloud is a distinct and separate service from the legacy cloud. Any desired data must be intentionally migrated from the legacy object storage to the new one, as management operations (creation, deletion, object manipulation, and key management) are controlled exclusively within their respective cloud environments.
What are the endpoint URLs for object storage on the legacy and new Arbutus Clouds?

The endpoint URL for the new Arbutus Cloud Object Storage is `https://object-arbutus.alliancecan.ca`. The endpoint URL for the legacy Arbutus Cloud Object Storage is `https://object-arbutus.cloud.computecanada.ca`.
What is the main purpose of this document regarding the Arbutus Cloud?
This document describes how to migrate virtual machine (VM) instances from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud.
Why is it necessary to migrate cloud resources from the legacy Arbutus Cloud?
Migration is necessary for all cloud resources currently on the legacy Arbutus Cloud because it will be decommissioned in 2026.
What is the deadline for all RAS and RAC projects to migrate to the new Arbutus Cloud?
The deadline for both RAS and RAC projects to migrate to the new Arbutus Cloud is August 31, 2026.
Who is primarily responsible for migrating instances from the legacy Arbutus Cloud to the new Arbutus Cloud?
Users are recommended to migrate their instances themselves, according to their own application requirements and schedule. Project owners are responsible for creating any necessary backups.
What key questions should users answer when planning their cloud migration from the legacy Arbutus Cloud?

Users should identify resources needing migration, determine if instances are volume-backed or ephemeral, identify volumes over 150 GB (for Globus), note if automation tools were used, check custom DNS entries, decide on OpenStack dashboard or CLI use, ensure active Alliance accounts, plan for outages, and for RAS projects, submit a migration request.
What are the URLs for accessing the legacy and new Arbutus Cloud OpenStack dashboards?
The legacy Arbutus Cloud URL is `https://arbutus.cloud.computecanada.ca`, and the new Arbutus Cloud URL is `https://arbutus.alliancecan.ca/`.
What preparatory steps are required before starting the migration to the new Arbutus Cloud?
Users must back up critical data, download and configure OpenStack RC files for both clouds, test RC file access, migrate SSH keys, migrate security groups and rules, and plan an outage window.
What specific lines must be added to the RC file downloaded from the new Arbutus Cloud?
Users must add `export OS_AUTH_TYPE=v3websso`, `export OS_IDENTITY_PROVIDER=atmosphere`, `export OS_PROTOCOL=openid`, and `export OS_PROJECT_DOMAIN_NAME=default`.
What are the three general migration scenarios outlined for the Arbutus Cloud?
The three general migration scenarios are Manual or Orchestrated migration, Migrating volume-backed instances, and Migrating ephemeral instances.
What method is recommended for migrating volume-backed instances with volumes less than 150 GB in the Arbutus Cloud?
Migration using Glance images is recommended for volume-backed instances with volumes less than 150 GB.
How are large volumes (over 150 GB) typically migrated from the legacy Arbutus Cloud?
For large volumes, copying data using rsync or the Linux 'dd' command is recommended, especially for bootable volumes, instead of image-based methods.
Which tools are recommended for copying data between instances in the two Arbutus Clouds, based on data volume size?
For very large volumes (e.g., greater than 5TB), Globus is recommended, while for small data volumes, rsync + ssh provides good transfer speeds.
What are the prerequisites for using Globus to transfer data between Arbutus Cloud instances?

Users need a Globus Connect Personal Plus subscription, Globus Connect Personal enabled on each cloud instance, VMs with external IP addresses, correct firewall rules, and the Globus Connect Personal user must have access to the data.
What post-transfer activities might be required after migrating data to the new Arbutus Cloud instances?

Post-transfer activities may include updating host-based firewall rules, updating DNS entries, updating IP addresses in configuration files, altering usernames in databases, and renewing TLS certificates.
How should users migrate data from the legacy CephFS shared filesystem to the new CephFS shared filesystem on the new Arbutus Cloud?
Users should create an equivalent share in the new cloud, mount both shares to separate locations on the same virtual machine in the new cloud, and then use `rsync` to transfer the data.
What is the recommended tool for migrating object storage data to the new Arbutus Cloud, and what is its main limitation?
Rclone is recommended, but it does not copy bucket ACLs, meaning all access will initially default to private in the new location.
Where can users get help if they encounter issues during the Arbutus Cloud migration process?
Support requests can be sent to `cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca`.
What is object storage and how does it differ from traditional storage architectures?

Object storage is a service that manages data as individual objects, rather than in a file hierarchy like traditional storage. A key difference is that objects cannot be edited in place; they must be created, replaced, or deleted as a whole unit. It is particularly effective for handling large files and numerous files, and is recommended for storing items that do not require hierarchical naming, are accessed mostly as a whole, are primarily read-only, and have simplified access-control rules.
What is the default allocation of object storage for Arbutus projects, and how can more be requested?

All Arbutus projects are initially allocated a default of 1TB of object storage. If more storage is required, an additional 9TB can be requested through the Rapid Access Service. For more than 10TB of object storage, a request must be submitted and allocated under the annual Resource Allocation Competition.
What are the key differences between using the Swift and S3 protocols for accessing the Arbutus Object Store?

How can a user make their Arbutus Object Store data container accessible to the public, and what are the implications of doing so?

How are access policies applied and viewed for data containers within the Arbutus Object Store?

What are the two main storage options available in OpenStack, and what are their characteristics regarding data protection?

OpenStack has two different storage options: Volumes, which are protected by 3 times replication against hardware failure but not accidental deletion or malicious data loss; and ephemeral storage local to the VM, which can suffer data loss due to hardware failure and should only be used for temporary or working data.
What is the best way to create a backup copy of a volume attached to a persistent virtual machine in OpenStack?

Why are OpenStack volume snapshots generally not ideal for backup purposes, and what are their primary uses?

OpenStack volume snapshots are not ideal for backups because they depend on the original volume remaining intact and cannot be downloaded. In OpenStack, how does backing up a Compute VM differ from a Persistent VM, and what type of data is not automatically captured in a Compute VM's image?

What are the key components of a good basic backup strategy for virtual machines with large disk images in OpenStack, and what is the most important final step in any backup plan?

For virtual machines with large disk images, a good basic strategy involves separating large datasets from the operating system and software stack. The OS and software can be backed up using a disk image or recreated with provisioning software, while datasets are backed up using file backup methods to a remote location. What is the procedure for attaching the CephFS network to a virtual machine (VM) on the SD4H/Juno OpenStack platform?

How do you attach the CephFS network to a virtual machine (VM) on SD4H/Juno using the OpenStack command-line client?

How do I install the CephFS client on a Red Hat Enterprise Linux family VM (e.g., RHEL, CentOS, Fedora, Rocky, Alma)?

To install the CephFS client on a Red Hat Enterprise Linux family VM, first add the Ceph software repository by creating `/etc/yum.repos.d/ceph.repo` with the appropriate content for your EL version (e.g., `el9` or `el10`), pointing to `http://download.ceph.com/rpm-tentacle/` for the latest stable release (as of June 2026, 'tentacle'). Next, install the Extra Packages for Enterprise Linux (EPEL) repository using `sudo dnf install epel-release`. If you're running EL10, temporarily disable the default cryptographic policy with `sudo update-crypto-policies --set LEGACY`. Then, import the Ceph project's public key using `sudo rpm --import 'https://download.ceph.com/keys/release.asc'`. Finally, install the client packages with `sudo dnf install -y libcephfs2 python3-cephfs ceph-common python3-ceph-argparse`. Remember to restore the default cryptographic policy on EL10 systems with `sudo update-crypto-policies --set DEFAULT` afterward.
What is the procedure for installing the CephFS client on a Debian-based VM (e.g., Debian, Ubuntu, Mint)?

To install the CephFS client on a Debian-based VM, first determine your distribution's codename using `lsb_release -sc`. Then, add the Ceph repository using `sudo apt-add-repository 'deb https://download.ceph.com/debian-tentacle/ {codename} main'`. If this command gives an error, revert it with `sudo add-apt-repository -r 'deb https://download.ceph.com/debian-tentacle/ {codename} main'`. After adding the repository, install the necessary CephFS client packages by running `sudo apt-get install -y libcephfs2 python3-cephfs ceph-common python3-ceph-argparse`.
After installing the Ceph client, which configuration files are required, and what essential information should they contain?

Two files are required: `ceph.conf` and `ceph.keyring`. The `ceph.conf` file contains global settings such as `admin socket`, `client reconnect stale`, `debug client`, `fuse big writes`, and critically, the `mon host` information specific to your cloud environment, along with `quota = true` under the `[client]` section. The `ceph.keyring` file must include your client name, typically formatted as `[client.MyCephFS-RW]`, and its corresponding `Access Key`.
How does one locate the client name and `Access Key` needed for the `ceph.keyring` file when configuring a CephFS client?

The client name and `Access Key` can be found under the access rules on your OpenStack project web page. To retrieve this information, navigate to `Project --> Share --> Shares`, and then click on the name of your specific share to view its details.
What are the distinct `mon host` configurations for the `ceph.conf` file when setting up a CephFS client on Arbutus versus SD4H/Juno cloud platforms?
How can a CephFS filesystem be permanently mounted on an OpenStack virtual machine (VM), and what are the specific considerations for Arbutus and SD4H/Juno platforms?

To permanently mount a CephFS filesystem, first create a mount point directory (e.g., `/cephfs`). Then, add an entry to the `/etc/fstab` file on your VM. For Arbutus, an example entry is `:/volumes/_nogroup/f6cb8f06-f0a4-4b88-b261-f8bd6b03582c /cephfs/ ceph name=MyCephFS-RW,nofail 0 2`. For SD4H/Juno, the entry requires additional options: `:/volumes/_nogroup/f6cb8f06-f0a4-4b88-b261-f8bd6b03582c /cephfs/ ceph name=MyCephFS-RW,mds_namespace=cephfs_4_2,x-systemd.device-timeout=30,x-systemd.mount-timeout=30,noatime,_netdev,rw,nofail 0 2`. Ensure you use the correct share path (starting with `:`) and client name from your share details, noting that the `nofail` option helps ensure system boot even if the CephFS service is unavailable.
What are the command-line instructions to directly mount a CephFS share on an OpenStack virtual machine (VM) for both Arbutus and SD4H/Juno platforms?

To directly mount a CephFS share from the command line, you must first create a mount point directory (e.g., `/cephfs`). For Arbutus, use `sudo mount -t ceph :/volumes/_nogroup/f6cb8f06-f0a4-4b88-b261-f8bd6b03582c /cephfs/ -o name=MyCephFS-RW`. For SD4H/Juno, the command includes additional mount options: `sudo mount -t ceph :/volumes/_nogroup/f6cb8f06-f0a4-4b88-b261-f8bd6b03582c /cephfs/ -o name=MyCephFS-RW,mds_namespace=cephfs_4_2,x-systemd.device-timeout=30,x-systemd.mount-timeout=30,noatime,_netdev,rw`. Ensure the share path and client name match your specific configuration.
How can a CephFS filesystem be mounted directly in user space using `ceph-fuse` on an OpenStack virtual machine (VM)?

To mount CephFS in user space using `ceph-fuse`, first install the `ceph-fuse` library by running `sudo dnf install ceph-fuse`. Next, uncomment the `user_allow_other` line in the `/etc/fuse.conf` file to allow user-space mounts. Finally, create a mount directory in your user's home (e.g., `~/my_cephfs`) and execute the command `ceph-fuse my_cephfs/ --id=MyCephFS-RW --conf=~/ceph.conf --keyring=~/ceph.keyring --client-mountpoint=/volumes/_nogroup/f6cb8f06-f0a4-4b88-b261-f8bd6b03582c`. The client name corresponds to the `--id`, and the `ceph.conf` and `ceph.keyring` files should contain the correct configuration and access key.
To which main category does this technical document belong?
This technical document belongs to the 'Cloud' category.
What is CephFS and its main purpose on Alliance OpenStack VM hosts?
CephFS provides a common filesystem that can be shared amongst multiple OpenStack VM hosts on Alliance clusters.
How do users request access to CephFS on Alliance clusters?
Users can request access to CephFS by sending an email to cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca.
What information is required when requesting a CephFS quota on Alliance clusters?
When requesting a CephFS quota, users need to provide their OpenStack project name, the amount of quota required (in GB), and the number of shares needed.
What foundational technical skills are assumed for setting up CephFS on OpenStack VMs?
Basic Linux skills are assumed, including creating and editing files, setting permissions, and creating mount points.
What are the key steps to create a CephFS share in the OpenStack Horizon GUI?

To create a share, navigate to 'Project --> Share --> Shares', click '+Create Share', then enter a share name, select 'CephFS' protocol, specify size, choose 'cephfs' (or 'cephfs-ec42' on SD4H/Juno) as share type, select 'nova' for availability zone, and ensure 'Make visible for all' is not checked.
How is an access rule created for a CephFS share within OpenStack, and what details are needed?

An access rule is created by going to 'Project --> Share --> Shares', selecting 'Manage Rules' from the Actions column, clicking '+Add Rule', then setting 'Access Type' to 'cephx', choosing 'read-write' or 'read-only' for 'Access Level', and defining an 'Access To' key name (e.g., MyCephFS-RW).
What three critical pieces of information from the CephFS share overview are needed for VM client configuration?
The three critical pieces of information are the share's 'Path', the 'Access to' (which is the client name), and the 'Access Key'.
How do you attach the CephFS network to a VM on Arbutus compared to SD4H/Juno in the Alliance OpenStack environment?

On Arbutus, the CephFS network is automatically exposed to VMs, so no action is needed. On SD4H/Juno, users must explicitly attach the 'CephFS-Network' to each VM via the Web GUI or the OpenStack command-line client.
How do users add the Ceph software repository for Red Hat Enterprise Linux family distributions (RHEL, CentOS, Fedora, Rocky, Alma) when configuring a CephFS client on an OpenStack VM?
Users must create or edit the '/etc/yum.repos.d/ceph.repo' file with the appropriate baseurl for their Enterprise Linux version (e.g., 'el9' or 'el10') pointing to 'download.ceph.com/rpm-tentacle/'.
What specific packages are needed for the CephFS client on RHEL-based systems when configuring it for an OpenStack VM?
The necessary packages are 'libcephfs2', 'python3-cephfs', 'ceph-common', and 'python3-ceph-argparse', which can be installed using `sudo dnf install -y`.
How do users add the Ceph software repository and install client packages on Debian-family distributions (Debian, Ubuntu, Mint) for CephFS client configuration on an OpenStack VM?

Users add the repository using `sudo apt-add-repository 'deb https://download.ceph.com/debian-tentacle/ {codename} main'` and then install packages with `sudo apt-get install -y libcephfs2 python3-cephfs ceph-common python3-ceph-argparse`.
What two main configuration files must be created or edited on an OpenStack VM for the CephFS client, and what information do they contain?

The two main files are '/etc/ceph/ceph.conf', containing global Ceph settings and 'mon host' details specific to Arbutus or SD4H/Juno, and '/etc/ceph/ceph.keyring', which stores the client name and access key.
Where can users find the monitor host (`mon host`) information for the `ceph.conf` file when configuring CephFS on Alliance OpenStack VMs?
The monitor host information is found in the 'Path' field within the share details on the OpenStack project web page (Project --> Share --> Shares, then click the share name).
How can CephFS be permanently mounted on an OpenStack VM using `/etc/fstab`, and what important option should be included?

CephFS can be permanently mounted by adding an entry to '/etc/fstab' with the share's path, mount point (e.g., '/cephfs/'), filesystem type 'ceph', and client name (e.g., 'name=MyCephFS-RW'). The 'nofail' option is important to ensure the system boots even if CephFS is unavailable.
How do you mount a CephFS share directly from the command line on an OpenStack VM?
To mount from the command line, use `sudo mount -t ceph :<share_path> <mount_point> -o name=<client_name>` (with additional options for SD4H/Juno like 'mds_namespace=cephfs_4_2').
How can CephFS be mounted in user space via `ceph-fuse` on an OpenStack VM, and what configuration adjustments are needed?

To mount in user space via `ceph-fuse`, install `ceph-fuse`, uncomment `user_allow_other` in '/etc/fuse.conf', and then use a command like `ceph-fuse ~/my_cephfs/ --id=MyCephFS-RW --conf=~/ceph.conf --keyring=~/ceph.keyring --client-mountpoint=<share_path>`.
Can a CephFS share on Alliance OpenStack clusters have multiple access keys, and what is the benefit of this feature?
Yes, a CephFS share can have more than one user key provisioned. This allows for more granular access control to the filesystem, such as providing read-only access to specific hosts.
Is the CephFS service available to hosts outside of the OpenStack cluster on Alliance?
No, the CephFS service is not available to hosts outside of the OpenStack cluster.
What type of service is provided, and what are the typical actions a user performs when utilizing the cloud infrastructure?

We offer Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) that supports virtualization. A user typically creates one or more virtual machines (VMs), logs in with administrative privileges, installs any desired software, and runs the necessary applications.
Under what circumstances should an individual opt for cloud services rather than using an HPC cluster?

It is preferable to work outside the cloud in an HPC environment if your work fits easily into the HPC batch submission workflow, as more resources are available and software is often pre-configured. The cloud is your solution if your specific need isn't served by Apptainer or HPC batch.
How does one obtain a cloud project, and what information must be provided when requesting a new project or an increase in quota?

To get a cloud project, you first need an account. If you are a primary investigator (PI) with an active cloud resource allocation, you should already have a project. Otherwise, you can request access to an existing project, a new project with our Rapid Access Service (RAS), or an increase in quota using the Alliance cloud project and RAS request form. For a new project or quota increase, you must provide justification including why you need cloud resources, why an HPC cluster is unsuitable, your plans for efficient resource usage, and your plans for maintenance and security.
What responsibilities do users have for their cloud projects?

For each cloud project, users are responsible for creating and managing their virtual machines (VMs), securing and patching software on their VMs, defining security groups to allow network access, creating user accounts, following best practices, considering security issues, and backing up their VMs.
Which cloud systems are available for users' projects?
Users' projects can be hosted on one of the following cloud systems: Béluga, Arbutus, Legacy Arbutus, Nibi, or Cedar.
What advanced functionalities are available for experienced cloud users, and what are some common cloud use cases?

More experienced users can automatically create virtual machines and describe their VM infrastructure as code using Terraform. Common cloud use cases include configuring a data or web server, utilizing vGPUs (standard shared GPU allocation or PCI-e passthrough), setting up a GUI Desktop on a VM, and using IPv6 in the Arbutus cloud.
What are the limitations for Primary Investigators (PIs) regarding cloud projects and resource quotas?
A Primary Investigator (PI) may own up to 3 projects, but the sum of all project quotas must be within the RAS allocation limits. PIs may also have both compute and persistent cloud RAS allocations.
Where can a user find instructions to manually create their first virtual machine on the cloud infrastructure?
The cloud quick start guide describes how to manually create your first VM.
What other resources should users consult when beginning to create virtual machines on the cloud infrastructure?
Users should review the Cloud Technical Glossary to learn definitions of common topics and consider cloud storage options best suited to their use case.
What kind of computing service does Alliance offer that supports virtualization?
Alliance offers Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) that supports virtualization.

The primary advantage is that the user has complete control over the collection of installed software, also known as the software stack.
What is a key disadvantage for a user when managing a virtual machine (VM) on Alliance's cloud infrastructure?
A key disadvantage is that the user must have some degree of experience in installing software and otherwise managing a computer.
When is it generally preferable to use an HPC cluster rather than Alliance's cloud service?

It is preferable to use an HPC cluster when your work fits easily into the HPC batch submission workflow and environment, as there are more resources available and software is often already configured.
What is a 'project' in the context of Alliance's cloud service?

How can a Primary Investigator (PI) request a new cloud project or an increase in an existing project's quota from Alliance?
A PI can request a new project or an increase in quota through the Alliance cloud project and RAS request form.

Justification is required, including why cloud resources are needed, why an HPC cluster is not suitable, plans for efficient resource usage, and plans for maintenance and security.
What is the typical processing time for cloud project requests submitted to Alliance?

Where can users find a guide to manually create their first virtual machine on Alliance's cloud infrastructure?

What tool can experienced users employ to describe their virtual machine infrastructure as code on Alliance's cloud?

Name some of the cloud systems available through Alliance.
Some of the cloud systems available are Béluga, Arbutus, Legacy Arbutus, Nibi, and Cedar.
What is the purpose of taking a 'snapshot' of a virtual machine in the Alliance cloud environment?
Taking a snapshot makes it easy to replicate or scale up a service and to recover from issues like power interruptions.
Who should users contact for assistance with Alliance's cloud service?
Users should contact technical support for questions about the cloud service.
What is Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM) is the process by which projects and accounts are provisioned and eventually deprovisioned throughout a lifecycle.
How is the specific type of lifecycle determined for projects and accounts under Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
The type of lifecycle for projects and accounts under CALM is tied to the type of allocation given to the Principal Investigator (PI) or group by CCDB or the Alliance.
What happens to CCDB accounts when a cloud project is provisioned?
Upon provisioning a cloud project, CCDB accounts are given roles which provide access to the project on the cloud infrastructure.
What is the definition of Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM) is the process by which projects and accounts are provisioned and eventually deprovisioned throughout a lifecycle.
Which entities does Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM) primarily manage throughout their lifecycle?
Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM) primarily manages projects and accounts.
What are the main actions performed on projects and accounts by Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
Projects and accounts are provisioned and eventually deprovisioned.
What factors determine the specific type of lifecycle used in Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
The type of lifecycle is tied to the type of allocation given to the PI/group by CCDB/the Alliance.
Who provides the allocation that determines the lifecycle type in Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
The allocation is provided by CCDB or the Alliance.
What happens to CCDB accounts when a cloud project is provisioned through Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
Upon provisioning a cloud project, CCDB accounts are given roles which provide access to the project on the cloud infrastructure.
What do the roles assigned to CCDB accounts enable them to do after a cloud project is provisioned?
The roles provide access to the project on the cloud infrastructure.
Where are 'local' accounts utilized within the cloud infrastructure described by this process?
'Local' accounts are used within virtual machines (VMs).
Are 'local' accounts included within the scope of Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
No, 'local' accounts are outside the scope of CALM.
What is the general scope of Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM)?
Cloud Account Lifecycle Management (CALM) manages the lifecycle of projects and accounts, which is tied to allocations provided by CCDB/the Alliance.
What are the initial requirements for accessing a cloud project?

To access a cloud project, users must first have an active cloud project associated with their account and use a compatible web browser such as Firefox or Chrome, as other browsers like some versions of Safari may not be supported and cause errors.
How do users log in to the cloud interface to access their OpenStack project?

Users can log in to the cloud interface by clicking the link provided in their confirmation email, opening it in a compatible web browser. They should then use their username (not email address) and password to access the OpenStack dashboard, which provides an overview of their project's resources.
Why are SSH key pairs necessary for Linux virtual machines (VMs) in OpenStack, and what are the methods for managing them?

SSH key pairs are necessary for Linux VMs because password authentication is disabled for security reasons; VMs are created with a public key installed, allowing login only with the corresponding SSH key pair. Users can either import an existing key pair or create a new one, with instructions available for Windows, Linux/Mac, or a general 'SSH Keys' page in the wiki for more information.
When creating a Windows virtual machine (VM) on OpenStack, which 'flavor' is recommended, and what are the minimum disk space requirements for the root drive?

For Windows VMs, the 'p2-3gb' flavor is recommended because Windows images are quite large and require a substantial bootable drive and sufficient RAM. The smallest 'p' flavor with 1.5 GB of RAM is generally insufficient for Windows. For the root drive, a device size of 30 GB or more should be entered, as the final operating system occupies approximately 20 GB, with additional space needed during setup.
After launching a new Windows virtual machine (VM) in OpenStack, what are the initial console-based steps required before the VM fully boots?

Once a Windows VM first boots, it will not finish the booting process until you select location, language, and keyboard settings and agree to the license agreement. These steps must be completed using the console built into the OpenStack dashboard, which can be accessed via the 'Console' tab on your VM's instance page.
When creating a new Windows virtual machine (VM) in OpenStack, what is the recommended setting for the 'Delete on Terminate' option for the volume?

It is generally recommended not to check the 'Delete on Terminate' box for the volume when creating a Windows VM. This allows the VM to be terminated without automatically deleting its associated volume, providing the option to delete the volume manually if desired and preventing accidental data loss.
How do you create a new SSH key pair for a Windows virtual machine using the OpenStack dashboard?

To create a new key pair for a Windows VM within the OpenStack dashboard, first click on 'Access & Security' from the left menu, then select the 'Key Pairs' tab. Next, click on the 'Create Key Pair' button, provide a name for your key pair, and click 'Create Key Pair' again. Finally, ensure you save the generated '.pem' file to your local drive.
How do you begin the process of launching a new virtual machine in the OpenStack interface?
To start creating a virtual machine, you need to click on the 'Instances' menu item located on the left side of the OpenStack interface, and then click the 'Launch Instance' button.
How do you navigate the console screen for a Windows VM if the mouse pointer is lagging?

If the mouse pointer is lagging on the Windows VM's console screen, you can use keyboard shortcuts. The 'tab' key selects different fields, and the 'up' and 'down' arrows select different options. For the 'Country or region' drop-down menu, letter keys move to the top of countries beginning with that letter. To proceed, press the 'tab' key until the 'next' box is selected, then press the 'enter' key.
What is the process for accepting the license agreement after a Windows VM has initially booted and locality settings are configured?

After configuring the locality settings on a Windows VM's console, you will be presented with a request to accept the terms and conditions of the license agreement. To do so, press the 'tab' key until the 'I accept' box is highlighted, then press the 'enter' key.
In an OpenStack project, what is the difference between a private IP address and a public IP address for a virtual machine?

In an OpenStack project, a private IP address (e.g., 192.168.X.Y) is assigned to a virtual machine (VM) from a local network within the project. This enables VMs to communicate with each other and with an internet gateway, but it does not allow external services or the outside world to initiate contact with the VM. A public IP address, conversely, permits outside services and tools to initiate contact with your VM, such as for performing administrative tasks, serving web content, or being referenced by domain names.
How do I assign a public IP address to a Windows virtual machine within an OpenStack project?

To assign a public IP address to a Windows virtual machine in an OpenStack project, navigate to the 'Instances' list. From the 'Actions' column for your VM, select 'Associate Floating IP' from the drop-down menu. If it's your first time, click the '+' sign in the 'Allocate Floating IP' dialogue box, then 'Allocate IP'. Finally, on the 'Manage Floating IP Associations' screen, click the 'Associate' button to complete the process.
What steps are required to configure the firewall to allow secure Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) connections to a Windows virtual machine in OpenStack?

To configure the firewall for secure RDP connections to a Windows virtual machine in OpenStack, first go to the 'Security Groups' tab and select 'Access & Security'. On the 'default' group row, click 'Manage Rules', then '+Add Rule'. Select 'RDP' from the 'Rules' dropdown menu. Crucially, replace the default 0.0.0.0/0 in the 'CIDR' text box with /32 (using your specific IP address, which can be found at ipv4.icanhazip.com) to restrict access. Leaving 0.0.0.0/0 is insecure and may lead to a cloud administrator revoking access. Finally, click the 'Add' button.
How do you retrieve the administrative password for a Windows virtual machine (VM) in OpenStack?

To retrieve the administrative password for a Windows VM, navigate to 'Instances' on the left menu in OpenStack. From the drop-down menu next to your instance, select 'Retrieve Password'. Then, click the 'Choose File' button to browse for and select your private key file (which should have a '.pem' extension and match the public key used during VM creation), and finally click the 'Decrypt Password' button at the bottom left.
What steps are required to connect to a Windows virtual machine (VM) from a Windows client using Remote Desktop Connection (RDC)?

To connect to a Windows VM from a Windows client using RDC, first open the Remote Desktop Connection tool. Enter the public IP address of your VM in the 'Computer' field and the provided user name in the 'User name' text box. Click 'Connect', then enter the decrypted password when prompted and click 'OK'. It is common to receive an alert about the remote computer's identity, which you should confirm by clicking 'Yes' to continue.
What are the format requirements for a private key used to decrypt a Windows virtual machine (VM) password in OpenStack?

For a private key to successfully decrypt a Windows VM password in OpenStack, it must be in OpenSSH format and not be protected by a passphrase. If you created your key pair using the OpenStack dashboard and downloaded the '.pem' file, or used the `ssh-keygen` command without specifying a passphrase, the key should be in the correct format.
What information is required to connect to a Windows virtual machine using a Remote Desktop Connection client?
To connect to a Windows virtual machine (VM) using a Remote Desktop Connection client, you need to supply a floating IP address, a user name, and a password.
What specific format requirements must an SSH private key meet to decrypt a Windows VM password in OpenStack?
To decrypt a Windows VM password in OpenStack, your SSH private key must be in OpenSSH format and must not have a passphrase.
How can users obtain an SSH private key in the correct format for connecting to a Windows VM created with OpenStack?

Users can obtain a correctly formatted SSH private key by either downloading the `.pem` file after creating a key pair directly within OpenStack, or by generating a key pair using the `ssh-keygen` command without specifying a passphrase.
What specific format must a private key adhere to for use in decrypting a Windows virtual machine password within OpenStack?
To decrypt a Windows VM password in OpenStack, your private key must be in OpenSSH format and must not be protected by a passphrase.
Which types of private key formats are not compatible with OpenStack for decrypting Windows virtual machine passwords?
OpenStack will not work with private keys in OpenSSH format that have a passphrase, nor will it work with keys in the ssh.com format, for decrypting Windows virtual machine passwords.
How do you import an existing SSH public key into an OpenStack cloud project?

To import an existing SSH public key into your OpenStack cloud project, navigate to "Compute" then "Key Pairs" in the left menu. Click on the "Import Public Key" button, provide a name for your key pair, and paste your public key (only RSA type SSH keys are currently supported). Ensure the pasted public key contains no newline or space characters, then click "Import Public Key". It is important to note that creating key pairs directly within OpenStack is not advised due to security issues arising from the absence of passphrases.
What are the initial steps and key considerations when launching a new virtual machine (VM) in OpenStack, specifically regarding its details and boot source?

To launch a new virtual machine (VM) in OpenStack, first select "Compute" then "Instances" from the left menu, and click the "Launch Instance" button. When configuring the VM:

*   **Details:** Enter a unique "Instance Name" without spaces or special characters. It's recommended to leave "Availability Zone" at its default and "Count" at 1 unless you have a specific plan for multiple machines.
*   **Source:** For a first VM, select "Image" as the boot source. Choose "Yes" for "Create New Volume" to ensure persistent storage for your VM's data, with a recommended "Volume Size" of 30 GB for the operating system and modest data needs. It's generally advised to click "No" for "Delete Volume on Instance Delete" to prevent accidental data loss. For Linux VMs, select a suitable image, such as the most recent Ubuntu, and remember your choice for future reference.
When launching a virtual machine (VM) in OpenStack, what does a 'Flavor' represent, and how do you select an appropriate one?

In OpenStack, a 'Flavor' defines the virtual machine's hardware specifications, including its allocated memory and processing capabilities. To select an appropriate flavor, navigate to the "Flavor" tab in the "Launch Instance" window. The "Available" list displays all flavors compatible with your chosen boot image. Click on the '>' icon next to a flavor to see how its specifications align with your project's resource allocations. You should choose a flavor that your project can support (i.e., one that does not show an alert icon for resource limitations) and then move it to the "Allocated" list using the upwards arrow.
When password authentication is disabled, what is the required method for logging into a virtual machine?
When password authentication is disabled, you can only log in to your virtual machine using an SSH key pair, which OpenStack installs on the VM.
What are the two primary approaches for managing SSH key pairs when setting up a virtual machine?

When setting up a virtual machine, you can either import an existing SSH public key from a key pair you've already created on another machine or create a new SSH key pair if you don't have one you wish to use.
If a user needs to create a new SSH key pair for a virtual machine, where should they look for instructions based on their local computer's operating system?

If you are using a Windows machine, consult the "Generating SSH keys in Windows" page for instructions. For Linux or Mac machines, follow the "Linux/Mac instructions." For more general information on creating and managing key pairs, refer to the "SSH Keys" page in the wiki.
What does a 'Flavor' determine for a virtual machine in the OpenStack cloud environment?
In the OpenStack cloud environment, the 'Flavor' determines the type of hardware that will be used for your virtual machine, thereby defining its memory and processing capabilities.
When launching a virtual machine in OpenStack, how can a user ensure they select a 'Flavor' that is compatible with their project's allocated resources?

To ensure compatibility, users should review the 'Available' list of 'Flavors'. An alert icon next to a specification for a particular 'Flavor' indicates that the project lacks sufficient resources to support it. Users should select a 'Flavor' that does not display an alert icon, meaning their project has the necessary resources.
After defining all options for a new virtual machine in OpenStack, what are the initial and final power states you can expect to see once it's launched?

After defining all options and clicking the 'Launch Instance' button, the virtual machine will be created. Initially, the 'Task' field for the VM will likely show 'Spawning'. Once the VM has spawned, its power state will transition to 'Running', which typically takes a few minutes.
In an OpenStack project, what are the two types of IP addresses a virtual machine can have, and what is the primary purpose of each?

A virtual machine in an OpenStack project can have a private IP address and, optionally, a public IP address. Private IP addresses (e.g., 192.168.X.Y) provide inter-VM networking within the project but do not allow for connections to the outside world. Public IP addresses enable outside services and tools to initiate contact with your VM, such as for administrative tasks, serving web content, or being pointed to by domain names.
What is the process for associating a public IP address (also known as a floating IP) with a virtual machine (VM) within an OpenStack project?

To associate a public IP address with a VM, ensure you are viewing the instances list. Click on the drop-down arrow menu on the far right of the VM's row and select 'Associate Floating IP'. In the 'Allocate Floating IP' window, click the 'Allocate IP' button. If this is your first time associating a floating IP, you will also need to click the '+' sign in the 'Manage Floating IP Associations' dialog box. Finally, click the 'Associate' button to complete the process. Your VM will then have both its private and public IP addresses listed.
After associating a public IP address with a virtual machine (VM), what changes should a user observe in the IP address column?
After associating a public IP address with a VM, the IP address column will display two IP addresses: one will be in the `192.168.X.Y` format (private IP), and the other will be the public IP.
Where can a user find a comprehensive list of their public IP addresses and the projects they are associated with within OpenStack?
A user can find a list of their public IP addresses and their associated projects by navigating to `Network->Floating IPs` in the OpenStack interface.
In OpenStack, what are the steps to configure the firewall to permit Secure Shell (SSH) access to a virtual machine (VM)?

To configure the firewall for SSH access to your VM in OpenStack, first navigate to 'Network->Security Groups' from the left menu. On the 'default' group row, click 'Manage Rules', then '+Add Rule'. In the 'Rule' drop-down menu, select 'SSH'. Replace `0.0.0.0/0` in the 'CIDR' text box with `your-ip/32`, using the IP address of your physical computer. You can find your current IP at ipv4.icanhazip.com. Finally, click 'Add'.

When connecting to an OpenStack virtual machine from a Linux or Mac computer, what is the required SSH command format, and what are the default usernames for popular image distributions like Ubuntu or Debian?

To connect from a Linux or Mac machine, open a terminal and use the command: `ssh -i /path/where/your/private/key/is/my_key.key <user name>@<public IP of your server>`. The default username depends on the image distribution: 'debian' for Debian, 'ubuntu' for Ubuntu, 'centos' for CentOS, 'fedora' for Fedora, 'almalinux' for AlmaLinux, and 'rocky' for Rocky. Ensure you have your private key and the VM's public IP address readily available.
How do you connect to a virtual machine (VM) using SSH from a Linux or Mac computer?

To connect to your virtual machine (VM) via SSH from a Linux or Mac computer, open a terminal and use the command: `ssh -i /path/where/your/private/key/is/my_key.key <user name>@<public IP of your server>`. In this command, `<user name>` is the name of the user connecting, and `<public IP of your VM>` is the public IP address you associated with your VM.
What are the default usernames for connecting to Linux virtual machines via SSH, based on their image distribution?
The default usernames for connecting to Linux virtual machines via SSH are as follows: for Debian, use `debian`; for Ubuntu, use `ubuntu`; and for CentOS, use `centos`.
What are the steps to connect to a virtual machine from a Windows computer using the MobaXterm application?

To connect to your virtual machine using MobaXterm, follow these instructions:
1. Open the MobaXterm application.
2. Click on "Sessions" then press "New session".
3. Select an SSH session.
4. Enter the public IP address for your VM in the "Remote host" address field.
5. Ensure that the "Specify username" checkbox is checked, then enter the image type for your VM (e.g., "ubuntu") into the username field, all lowercase.
6. Click on the "Advanced SSH settings" tab, and check the "Use private key" checkbox.
7. Click on the page icon in the far right of the "Use private key" field. In the pop-up dialogue box, select the key pair (.pem file) that you saved to your computer.
8. Then click on OK. MobaXterm will save that session information for future connections, open an SSH connection to your VM, and also open an SFTP connection for file transfers via the left-hand panel.
When connecting to a Linux virtual machine via SSH, what are the default usernames for different image distributions like Debian, Ubuntu, CentOS, Fedora, AlmaLinux, and Rocky?

When connecting to a Linux virtual machine via SSH, the default usernames depend on the image distribution:
* Debian: `debian`
* Ubuntu: `ubuntu`
* CentOS: `centos`
* Fedora: `fedora`
* AlmaLinux: `almalinux`
* Rocky: `rocky`
These default users have full sudo privileges, and connecting directly to the root account via SSH is disabled.
When creating a Windows virtual machine, what is the recommended method for generating an SSH key pair, and what are the steps to do so within the OpenStack dashboard?

For Windows virtual machines, it is recommended to create a new key pair within the OpenStack dashboard rather than importing an existing key pair. To create a new key pair:
1. Click on 'Access & Security' from the left menu.
2. Select the 'Key Pairs' tab.
3. Click on the 'Create Key Pair' button; the 'Create Key Pair' window is displayed.
4. Give your key pair a name.
5. Click the 'Create Key Pair' button again.
6. Save the generated `<key name>.pem` file on your local drive. This key pair is used to encrypt the administrative account password for the Windows VM, which the matching private key decrypts.
What is a prerequisite for accessing a cloud project on Alliance clusters?
You must first have a cloud project associated with your account, and you will receive a confirmation email with important access details after it's set up.
Which web browsers are recommended for accessing the cloud interface for Alliance clusters, and why?
Firefox and Chrome are recommended because other browsers, like certain versions of Safari, may not be fully supported and can cause submission errors.
How do users log in to their cloud project interface on Alliance clusters?
Users log in using the link provided in their confirmation email, entering their username (not email address) and password.
When creating a virtual machine on Alliance clusters, what is an important distinction to remember regarding the operating system choice?
Users should remember that the chosen operating system is for the virtual machine (instance), not the physical computer they are using to connect.
How is authentication handled for Linux virtual machines created on Alliance clusters?
Password authentication is disabled for security reasons; users must log in using an SSH (Secure Shell) key pair.
What is the recommended method for handling SSH key pairs for Linux VMs in OpenStack on Alliance clusters?

It is recommended to either import an existing SSH public key or create a new key pair outside of OpenStack, as creating key pairs within OpenStack is not advised due to security concerns (no passphrase).
What are the critical configuration steps when launching a Linux VM instance in OpenStack on Alliance clusters?

How do users assign a public IP address to their Linux VM on Alliance clusters?
From the 'Instances' list, select 'Associate Floating IP' from the VM's drop-down menu, then click 'Allocate IP' and 'Associate'.
How do users configure the firewall to allow SSH access to their Linux VM from their personal computer on Alliance clusters?

What are key considerations for "Flavor" and "Device Size" when launching a Windows VM on Alliance clusters?

How do users configure the firewall to allow Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) access to their Windows VM on Alliance clusters?

How do users retrieve the administrative password for a Windows VM on Alliance clusters?
Go to 'Instances', select 'Retrieve Password' from the VM's drop-down menu, choose the private key file, and click 'Decrypt Password'.
What is the Rapid Access Service (RAS) provided by the Digital Research Alliance of Canada, and who is eligible to use it?

The Rapid Access Service (RAS) allows any Digital Research Alliance of Canada user with an Alliance account to access modest quantities of resources immediately for experimentation and starting work. Many research groups can meet their needs with RAS alone. Primary Investigators (PIs) with a current Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) allocation are also able to request resources via RAS.
What are the two main types of cloud instances available through the Digital Research Alliance of Canada, and how do they differ in their intended use and characteristics?

The two main types of cloud instances are Compute instances and Persistent instances. Compute instances have a limited life-time (maximum one month wall-time), typically require constant high CPU, and are used for production activities or batch processing, with owners notified for cleanup upon deactivation. Persistent instances are designed to run indefinitely, often for services like Web or database servers, and generally use less CPU power than compute instances.
What vGPU options are currently available for Rapid Access Service (RAS) users on the Arbutus platform, and what are their specifications?

For Rapid Access Service (RAS) users on the Arbutus platform, H100 GPUs are currently offered in a single flavour: 'g1-12gb-c3-35gb-125'. This specific vGPU flavour provides 12GB of GPU memory, 3 vCPUs, 35GB of system memory, and 125GB of ephemeral storage.
How can a user request a Cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) allocation?
Users can request a Cloud RAS allocation by filling out the Google Form provided on the Digital Research Alliance of Canada's website.
For Cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS), which resource quotas are considered 'soft limits' and can be increased without a Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) request?

The quotas for instances, volumes, and volume snapshots are metadata quotas, not hard limits. Users can request an increase beyond these default values without needing a Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) request.
What are the default duration and renewal policies for Cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) Compute and Persistent instances?

Both Compute and Persistent instances have a default duration of one year, with renewals typically taking effect in April. Compute instances also have a one-month wall-time limit. Primary Investigators (PIs) may request one-year renewals an unlimited number of times, but these allocations are based on available resources and are not guaranteed.
What is the purpose of the Rapid Access Service (RAS) for Digital Research Alliance of Canada users?
The Rapid Access Service (RAS) allows any Digital Research Alliance of Canada user to access modest quantities of resources immediately for experimentation and to begin working right away.

How does the Rapid Access Service (RAS) differ from the Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) for Digital Research Alliance of Canada users?
RAS allows immediate access to modest resources for experimentation, while RAC is for users requiring larger resource quantities and involves an annual application process.
