Only Primary Investigators (PIs) are permitted to request both compute and persistent cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) allocations.
Can compute and persistent cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) allocations share resources like project and storage?
Yes, PIs may request both a compute and persistent allocation to share a single project, and storage is shared between the two allocations.
How often can PIs renew their cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) allocations, and when do renewals typically take effect?
PIs may request a one-year renewal an unlimited number of times, and renewals generally take effect in April.
What are the vCPU limits for compute and persistent instances under the cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS)?
The vCPU limit for compute instances is 80, and for persistent instances, it is 25.
What are the maximum storage limits for persistent, object, and shared filesystem storage for cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) users?

Are the instance and volume limits for cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) strict, or can they be increased?
These are metadata quotas (soft limits), and users can request an increase beyond these values without a Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) request.
What is the default duration for cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) allocations?
The default duration for both compute and persistent cloud Rapid Access Service (RAS) allocations is one year.
What is the maximum wall-time for compute instances provisioned through the Digital Research Alliance of Canada's Rapid Access Service (RAS)?
The maximum wall-time for compute instances is one month.
How does a user request access to the Digital Research Alliance of Canada's Rapid Access Service (RAS)?
Users can request RAS by filling out the specified Google Form.

The RAM limit for compute instances is 300 GB, and for persistent instances, it is 50 GB.

In Canada's advanced research computing environment, what is the distinction between 'security in the cloud' and 'security of the cloud,' and who is responsible for each?

'Security in the cloud' is the responsibility of the research teams, focusing on protecting their research data, virtual machines, operating systems, services, and applications. 'Security of the cloud' is the responsibility of the cloud support team, focusing on protecting the underlying cloud platforms, including compute, storage, database, and networking capabilities.
What are the key security responsibilities for research teams using cloud platforms in Canada's advanced research computing environment?

Research teams are responsible for implementing security controls to protect their research data's confidentiality, integrity, and availability. This includes installing, configuring, and managing their virtual machines, operating systems, services, and applications; applying timely updates and security patches; configuring security group rules; implementing and testing backup and recovery procedures; encrypting sensitive data; and following the principle of least privilege when granting access.
What are the primary responsibilities of the cloud support team regarding 'security of the cloud,' and what is their policy on managing virtual machines?

The cloud support team is responsible for protecting the cloud platforms, configuring and managing compute, storage, database, and networking capabilities, applying timely updates to the cloud platform, maintaining logs for investigations, and ensuring the environmental and physical security of the cloud infrastructure. While the team does not support or manage virtual machines, they may shut down and lock a VM if it adversely impacts others, requiring the research team to provide remediation plans before access is restored.
What is the main purpose of this document regarding Canada's advanced research computing environment?

This document describes the responsibilities of the cloud team who administers cloud platforms, the research teams who use these platforms, and the shared responsibilities between both, specifically focusing on security.
Who is responsible for 'Security in the cloud' within Canada's advanced research computing environment?
Research teams are responsible for 'Security in the cloud', which involves protecting their research data and managing their virtual machines and applications.
Who is responsible for 'Security of the cloud' within Canada's advanced research computing environment?
Our cloud support team is responsible for 'Security of the cloud', which involves protecting the underlying cloud platforms and their infrastructure.
What are some key security responsibilities of research teams when using cloud platforms?

Research teams are responsible for implementing security controls for data, managing virtual machines and their operating systems, applying updates and patches, configuring security group rules, implementing backup and recovery, encrypting sensitive data, and following the principle of least privilege.
What are the primary responsibilities of our cloud support team for the cloud platforms?

Our cloud support team is responsible for protecting the cloud platforms, configuring and managing compute, storage, database, and networking capabilities, applying platform updates and patches, maintaining logs for investigations, and ensuring the environmental and physical security of the cloud infrastructure.
Does our cloud support team manage virtual machines for research teams?
No, our cloud support team does not support or manage virtual machines. However, they may shut down and lock a virtual machine if it adversely impacts others.
What kind of updates and patches are research teams responsible for applying?
Research teams are responsible for applying updates and security patches on a timely basis to their virtual machines, operating systems, services, and applications.
What specific actions should research teams take regarding data encryption on cloud platforms?
Research teams should encrypt sensitive data both in transit and at rest to protect its confidentiality and integrity.
What principle should research teams follow when granting access to their cloud resources?
Research teams should follow the principle of least privilege when granting access to ensure users have only the necessary permissions.
What are the shared responsibilities between our cloud support team and research teams?

Compliance is a shared responsibility, requiring both teams to comply with applicable laws, policies, procedures, contracts, and particularly the Alliance Federation Terms of Use, and to be 'good Net citizens'.
What could happen if a virtual machine adversely impacts others on the cloud platform?
If a virtual machine adversely impacts others, our cloud support team may shut it down and lock it. The research team may then be asked to provide remediation plans before access is restored.
Where can research teams find more information about cloud security considerations for their specific needs?
Research teams can refer to the 'Cloud security considerations for research teams' resource mentioned in the document for more information.
What contact email is provided for questions about the cloud security responsibility model described in the document?
For any questions about this model, users can contact cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca.
What is the importance of being 'good Net citizens' when using Alliance cloud services?
Being 'good Net citizens' is important to protect the reputation of the networks and prevent all users from being blocked or banned from the services.
What specific policy document from the Alliance Federation is highlighted as requiring compliance for cloud service users?
Compliance is particularly required with respect to the Alliance Federation Terms of Use.
What are the distinct types of storage options available within our cloud environments?

Our cloud environments offer four primary storage types: Volume storage (the standard unit, attachable/detachable from an instance), Ephemeral/Disk storage (virtual local disk tied to a single instance's lifecycle), Object storage (non-hierarchical, for whole-file uploads), and Shared filesystem storage (private network attached, configurable on each mounted instance).
Which specific storage type can be mounted on multiple virtual machines simultaneously and also provides automatic backups?
Shared filesystem storage is the type that can be mounted on multiple virtual machines (VMs) simultaneously, even across different projects, and it also includes automatic nightly backups to tape.
Which storage type is automatically deleted when its associated virtual machine is removed, and what is its primary use?

Ephemeral/Disk storage is automatically deleted upon the deletion of its associated virtual machine. It is primarily suitable for temporary data because it is virtual local disk storage tied to the lifecycle of a single instance, and 'c' flavour local disks can be lost.
What are the different types of storage available in the described cloud environments?
The available storage types are Volume storage, Ephemeral/Disk storage, Object storage, and Shared filesystem storage.
What is Volume storage in the context of cloud computing?
Volume storage is the standard storage unit for cloud computing that can be attached to and detached from an instance.
How is Ephemeral/Disk storage characterized in cloud environments?
Ephemeral/Disk storage is virtual local disk storage tied to the lifecycle of a single instance on a hypervisor's local disk, where 'c' flavor local disk can be lost.
What is Object storage, as described for cloud environments?
Object storage is a non-hierarchical storage type where data is created or uploaded in whole-file form.
What is Shared filesystem storage in a cloud environment?
Shared filesystem storage is private network-attached storage space, similar to NFS/SMB shares, which must be configured on each instance where it is mounted.
Which storage types are considered the default options in the described cloud environments?
Volume storage and Ephemeral/Disk storage are the default storage options.
Can any of the described cloud storage types be accessed via a web browser?
Yes, Object storage can be accessed via a web browser.
Which cloud storage type allows for access restriction based on specific source IP ranges?
Object storage allows access restriction for specific source IP ranges using S3 ACL.
Which storage type can be mounted on multiple VMs simultaneously, even across projects?
Only Shared filesystem storage can be mounted on multiple VMs (and across projects) simultaneously.
Does any of the cloud storage types offer automatic backups?
Yes, Shared filesystem storage offers automatic nightly backups to tape.
Which storage types are suitable for data or files that change frequently in the cloud?
Volume storage, Ephemeral/Disk storage, and Shared filesystem storage are suitable for data/files that change frequently.
Which of the described cloud storage types feature a hierarchical filesystem?
Volume storage, Ephemeral/Disk storage, and Shared filesystem storage feature a hierarchical filesystem.
Is Ephemeral/Disk storage suitable for long-term data retention in the cloud?
No, Ephemeral/Disk storage is not suitable for long-term storage.
Which storage type is automatically deleted when its associated Virtual Machine (VM) is deleted?
Ephemeral/Disk storage is deleted automatically upon deletion of a VM.
What is the standard magnitude of allocation for Object storage and Shared filesystem storage?
The standard magnitude of allocation for Object storage and Shared filesystem storage is TB.
Do any of the described cloud storage types provide physical disk-level encryption?
No, none of the described storage types provide physical disk-level encryption.
Which storage types offer multi-disk fault tolerance?
Volume storage, Object storage, and Shared filesystem storage offer multi-disk fault tolerance. For Ephemeral/Disk storage, 'c-flavors' do not, but 'p-flavors' do.
What is the difference between 'compute cloud' and 'persistent cloud' resources in our infrastructure?

Compute cloud resources are allocated to support OpenStack instances intended to run for a limited time, usually with very high sustained usage of CPU and memory. Their flavours have labels beginning with 'c*'. Persistent cloud resources are an allocation type for virtual machines expected to run indefinitely with low or bursty CPU requirements. Their flavours have labels beginning with 'p*'. Both types are currently available on Arbutus, Béluga, and Cedar.
What is the primary function of OpenStack within our cloud infrastructure?
OpenStack is the software suite used on our clouds to control hardware resources such as computers, storage, and networking.
What is object storage and which protocols are supported in our cloud services?

Object storage is a type of storage that manages data as objects, with each object typically including the data itself, variable metadata, and a globally unique identifier. It is offered as S3 and Swift protocols and is currently only available with Arbutus.
What is a security group, and how is it used in cloud environments?
A security group is a collection of security rules designed to control network traffic. It can be applied as a whole to one or more OpenStack instances to manage their network access.
What defines a service portal in our infrastructure, and what are its common characteristics?

A service portal is a Web research portal hosted by our infrastructure that provides datasets or tools to a wide research community. These portals typically require a public IP address, may have stricter up-time requirements than standard research projects, and often use our cloud resources, though they generally don't demand extensive computing or storage.
What is a shared filesystem in the cloud environment, and what are its key characteristics?

A shared filesystem is a persistent storage space, compliant with Unix standards, that can be mounted across multiple hosts within a project to facilitate data sharing. This service runs on CephFS and requires either a Fuse driver (for Windows/Linux) or the CephFS kernel driver (for Linux) for access. It is allocated in terabytes (TB).
What is the primary function of a snapshot within an OpenStack environment?
A snapshot is a copy of an OpenStack volume. Its primary function is to serve as a backup for the volume or to be used to launch another OpenStack instance.
What is volume storage in the cloud, and how is it implemented?

Volume storage is a type of persistent cloud storage that provides virtual disk functionality to OpenStack instances running in the cloud. It is implemented using Ceph software and is typically allocated in gigabytes (GB).
What does CALM stand for and what is its primary function in relation to cloud resources?
CALM stands for cloud account lifecycle management, and its primary function is managing the allocation of cloud resources.
What is Ceph, and what type of storage does it provide for the Alliance's clouds?
Ceph is a distributed data storage platform used for the Alliance's clouds, and it includes volume storage.
What is CephFS, and which specific cloud cluster currently offers this file system?
CephFS (Ceph File System) is a file system with Ceph storage that allows data to be mounted simultaneously on multiple OpenStack instances. It is currently only available with Arbutus.
What is the key difference between a 'compute cloud' and a 'persistent cloud' allocation type on Alliance clusters?

A 'compute cloud' allocation supports OpenStack instances for a limited time with high, sustained CPU and memory usage (c* flavours), while a 'persistent cloud' allocation is for virtual machines expected to run indefinitely with low or bursty CPU requirements (p* flavours).
What is CVMFS primarily used for in the context of cloud services?
CVMFS (CernVM File System) is a read-only content distribution system often used to manage software.
How is an 'ephemeral local disk' created for an OpenStack instance, and when is it destroyed?
An ephemeral local disk is created when an OpenStack instance is launched without the specification of a volume, and it is destroyed along with the instance.
What is a 'flavor' in OpenStack terminology?
A 'flavor' is an OpenStack term for a predefined specification for a new instance, which can define sizes for RAM, disk, and the number of cores.
What is the purpose of a 'floating IP' for an OpenStack instance?
A 'floating IP' is an Internet Protocol address that can be associated with an OpenStack instance to allow external access.
What is Horizon, and how does it facilitate the management of OpenStack cloud resources?
Horizon is the OpenStack cloud dashboard that is used for viewing and managing cloud resources through a web browser.
What is 'object storage' and which protocols are offered for it on the Alliance's cloud infrastructure?
Object storage is a storage type that manages data as objects, including data, metadata, and a unique identifier. It is offered as S3 and Swift protocols, currently only with Arbutus.
What is OpenStack, and what hardware resources does it control on the Alliance's clouds?
OpenStack is the software suite used on the Alliance's clouds to control hardware resources such as computers, storage, and networking.
What is the Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) and who evaluates the requests?

The Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) is a program where Principal Investigators can submit requests for storage and computer resources beyond what is available via the Rapid Access Service, with requests evaluated by a committee of peers.
What is the Rapid Access Service (RAS) for researchers?
The Rapid Access Service (RAS) allows Principal Investigators to request a modest amount of storage and cloud resources without having to apply to the Resource Allocation Competition (RAC).
What is a 'security group' in the context of OpenStack, and what is its function?
A 'security group' is a set of security rules that control network traffic and can be applied as a whole to one or more OpenStack instances.
What is a 'shared filesystem' and for what purpose is it typically used across multiple hosts in a project?
A 'shared filesystem' is a persistent, Unix-compliant storage space that can be mounted across multiple hosts in a project, making it useful for sharing data.
What does vCPU stand for, and what does it represent in a virtual machine?
vCPU stands for virtual central processing unit, and it represents a portion or share of the underlying, physical CPU that is assigned to a particular virtual machine.
What is a 'volume' in OpenStack, and how does it function like a virtual disk?
A 'volume' is a storage resource that can be attached to or detached from an OpenStack instance, functioning like a virtual disk.
What is 'volume storage' and how is it implemented and allocated in the Alliance's cloud?
Volume storage is a type of persistent cloud storage that provides virtual disk functionality to OpenStack instances running in the cloud. It is implemented with Ceph software and allocated in GB.
What is the primary requirement for logging into the cloud service, and what error message indicates this requirement hasn't been met?
To log in to the cloud service, you must specifically apply for and be granted a cloud project. If you haven't, you will receive an "Invalid Credentials" error message upon attempting to log in.
After being granted a cloud project, what steps should a user take if they are unable to log in to the cloud service?

If you have a confirmed cloud project but can't log in, first ensure you're using the correct login link for your project's host cloud. Then, check the System status page for any service incidents. Make sure you're using your HPC cluster username (not your email address), and if your password is rejected, reset it using the provided link. If the issue persists, submit a ticket to cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca with your username, project name, the cloud you're trying to access, and the steps you've already taken.
What are two common reasons a virtual machine (VM) might fail to launch, and how can these issues be addressed?

A VM might fail to launch if it exceeds your cloud project's resource limits (quotas) for VMs, CPUs, or RAM. You can check your usage on the cloud dashboard under "Compute" and then "Overview"; if you need more resources, request them using the provided form. Another common error is "No valid host was found," which often occurs when an inappropriate Availability Zone is manually selected during launch. This can usually be resolved by setting the Availability Zone back to "Any Availability Zone".
What are the initial steps to troubleshoot if you cannot connect to your virtual machine or a service it is running?

First, check the System Status page to see if there is an incident affecting service on your hosting cloud. If no incident is reported, try to log in to the OpenStack dashboard for your cloud project. If you cannot reach the login page for your cloud, verify your internet connectivity by attempting to access a website like Google.
If you are encountering a 'not enough hosts' error when trying to launch a virtual machine, or if your instance still won't boot after initial troubleshooting, what is the next step?

If you continue to get the 'not enough hosts' error, or if your instance won't boot after following previous troubleshooting steps, you should submit a ticket to cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca. Include your username, project name, cloud name, and any information you collected during your troubleshooting process.
If your virtual machine is running but you are unable to connect to it using SSH, what troubleshooting steps should you follow?

First, verify you are using the correct key pair and username for your VM's operating system (e.g., 'debian' for Debian, 'ubuntu' for Ubuntu, 'almalinux' for AlmaLinux, 'centos' for CentOS, 'fedora' for Fedora). If you do not get a login prompt, check your security settings to ensure your current IP address is unblocked for SSH connections (Port 22). You can verify your IP address at https://ipv4.icanhazip.com/ and then ensure it's added as a rule in your VM's security group.
What might cause the error message 'Error: No valid host was found. There are not enough hosts available.' when launching a virtual machine instance?
This error can occur if you manually select an Availability Zone when trying to launch the instance, instead of using the default 'Any Availability Zone' option.
How can a user resolve the 'No valid host was found. There are not enough hosts available.' error if it's caused by an Availability Zone selection?
To resolve this error, you should set the Availability Zone back to 'Any Availability Zone' when configuring the instance details.
How can I find instructions for connecting to my virtual machine using SSH?

You can find instructions for connecting to your virtual machine with SSH in the 'Cloud Quick Start Guide', specifically in the section titled 'Connecting to your VM with SSH' located near the bottom of the page.
Where can I verify which SSH key pair I should use to connect to my virtual machine?

To check which key pair you should be using for your virtual machine, click on 'Compute' in the left-side menu of the OpenStack page, then select 'Instances', and then look for the column titled 'Key Pair'.
Does the username for connecting to a virtual machine via SSH vary?
Yes, the correct username for connecting to your virtual machine via SSH depends on the operating system of the VM.
What are the default SSH usernames for virtual machines running various operating systems?

The default SSH usernames depend on the operating system of the virtual machine:
- Debian: debian
- Ubuntu: ubuntu
- AlmaLinux: almalinux
- CentOS: centos
- Fedora: fedora
(Note: This table does not apply if you explicitly changed your username with a custom CloudInit script.)
If a user cannot connect to their virtual machine via SSH, what security settings should they verify?

Users should verify two security settings: first, that their own IP address has not changed and is allowed in the security settings. They can check their IP address using a service like https://ipv4.icanhazip.com/. Second, they should check their security group rules to ensure that their current IP address is unblocked for SSH connections (Port 22, TCP protocol, Ingress direction) to their virtual machine. If their IP has changed or the rule is missing, they need to add or update the rule in the security group settings.
What are the common reasons why a user might be unable to delete a volume in the cloud service?

A user might be unable to delete a volume for a few common reasons:
1. The volume is attached to a running virtual machine (VM). It must be detached before it can be deleted.
2. The volume's status is still listed as 'In-use' even after being detached, indicating a potential system issue.
3. There are snapshots of the volume that still exist. All snapshots of a volume must be deleted before the source volume can be removed.

What is the primary reason to use encryption like Transport Layer Security (TLS) or Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) for web servers?

Using TLS/SSL encryption for web server communication is crucial for protecting sensitive information, such as passwords, during transmission over the internet. It also prevents third parties from intercepting and modifying any data sent between the web server and the client, even if the information isn't sensitive.
What are the two main types of SSL certificates, and which one is generally recommended for public-facing websites?

The two main types of certificates are those signed by a third-party signing authority and self-signed certificates. For public-facing sites, a certificate signed by a third party, such as one obtained easily using Let's Encrypt, is recommended. Self-signed certificates should not be used for production sites, as visitors will receive a security warning because no third party vouches for the server's validity; they are primarily useful for testing or small, locally used sites.
On an Ubuntu operating system with Apache, what are the initial steps to activate the SSL module and generate a self-signed SSL certificate?

First, activate the SSL module using the commands `sudo a2enmod ssl` and `sudo service apache2 restart`. Then, create a self-signed SSL certificate by executing `sudo openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout /etc/ssl/private/server.key -out /etc/ssl/certs/server.crt`. Ensure the `-nodes` option is used to avoid being prompted for a passphrase, and be prepared to answer a series of questions, including the 'Common Name' which should be your server's domain name or public IP.
When creating a self-signed SSL certificate, what information should be used for the "Common Name" when the server is a virtual machine on a cloud?
For a virtual machine on a cloud, the "Common Name" during self-signed SSL certificate creation should be the floating IP address associated with that virtual machine.
How does one configure Apache to utilize a newly generated self-signed SSL certificate for encrypted communications?

To configure Apache, edit the `/etc/apache2/sites-available/default-ssl.conf` file. The lines `SSLCertificateFile` and `SSLCertificateKeyFile` must be updated to reference `/etc/ssl/certs/server.crt` and `/etc/ssl/private/server.key`, respectively. You should also add `SSLCertificateChainFile /etc/ssl/certs/server.crt`. Additionally, ensure that the `DocumentRoot` variables are identical between `default-ssl.conf` and `000-default.conf`.
What steps are involved in tightening security and enabling an Apache web server to force HTTPS traffic after configuring it with a self-signed SSL certificate?

First, edit `/etc/apache2/sites-available/default-ssl.conf` to specify the `ServerName` (using the VM's public IP), disable older SSL protocols (like SSLv2 and SSLv3 with `SSLProtocol all -SSLv2 -SSLv3`), and define a strong `SSLCipherSuite` along with `SSLHonorCipherOrder on`. Next, modify `/etc/apache2/sites-available/000-default.conf` to add a permanent redirect from HTTP to HTTPS within the `<VirtualHost>` tag. Finally, enable the SSL-configured site using `sudo a2ensite default-ssl.conf` and restart the Apache service with `sudo service apache2 restart`.
What information does the `openssl req` command prompt for when generating a self-signed SSL certificate on an Ubuntu operating system?

When generating a self-signed SSL certificate, the `openssl req` command prompts for the following information: Country Name (2 letter code), State or Province Name (full name), Locality Name (e.g., city), Organization Name (e.g., company), Organizational Unit Name (e.g., section), Common Name (e.g., server FQDN or YOUR name), and Email Address. Example responses provided include 'CA' for Country, 'Nova Scotia' for State, 'Halifax' for Locality, 'Alliance' for Organization, 'ACENET' for Organizational Unit, 'XXX-XXX-XXX-XXX.cloud.computecanada.ca' for Common Name, and '<your email>' for Email Address.
When creating a self-signed SSL certificate using the `openssl req` command, which field is the most important to complete, and what should be provided for a virtual machine on a cloud?

The 'Common Name' is the most important field to complete. For a virtual machine on a cloud, it should be the domain name of your server, similar to the example `XXX-XXX-XXX-XXX.cloud.computecanada.ca`, where the string of 'Xs' is replaced with the floating IP associated with the virtual machine.
What is the main purpose of the section on Transport Layer Security (TLS) and Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) within the 'Creating a web server on a cloud' page?

The main purpose is to explain the importance of using encryption (TLS/SSL) for web server communications over the internet and to provide guidance on implementing it, primarily focusing on Apache web servers.
Why is it important to use encryption, such as Transport Layer Security (TLS) or Secure Sockets Layer (SSL), for web server communications?
Encryption is crucial for protecting sensitive information like passwords and for preventing third parties from intercepting or modifying data sent between a web server and a client.
What are the two main types of SSL certificates discussed for web servers?
The two main types are certificates signed by a third-party signing authority and self-signed certificates.
What is the primary advantage of using a certificate signed by a third-party Certificate Authority (CA) over a self-signed certificate for a web server?

A CA-signed certificate allows visitors to verify they are accessing the correct website, preventing man-in-the-middle attacks, and avoids security warnings in web browsers that self-signed certificates typically trigger.
When might a self-signed SSL certificate be a suitable option for a web server?
Self-signed certificates may be suitable for testing purposes or for small, locally used sites where public trust and third-party validation are not critical.
What is Let's Encrypt and how does it relate to obtaining SSL certificates for web servers?
Let's Encrypt is a Certificate Authority (CA) that provides free SSL certificates. It is recommended for easily obtaining third-party signed certificates.
What tool is recommended to automatically create or renew a Let's Encrypt SSL certificate and configure a web server to use it?
Certbot is the recommended tool for automatically managing Let's Encrypt SSL certificates and configuring them with your web server.
What specific network port needs to be opened for Certbot to connect to a site if you are configuring it via Apache?
Port 443 (TCP ingress) must be opened for Certbot to connect to the site when configuring it through Apache.
What operating system is assumed for the procedure to create a self-signed SSL certificate for an Apache web server?
The procedures for creating a self-signed SSL certificate assume the use of the Ubuntu operating system.
What is the command to activate the SSL module for an Apache web server on Ubuntu?
The command to activate the SSL module for Apache on Ubuntu is `sudo a2enmod ssl`, followed by `sudo service apache2 restart`.
When creating a self-signed SSL certificate using the `openssl` command, which question is considered the most important to answer correctly?
The "Common Name (e.g. server FQDN or YOUR name)" question is the most important, as it should be the domain name or public IP of your server.
After creating a self-signed SSL certificate and private key, what steps are necessary to set correct ownership and permissions for the private key file on an Apache web server?
You need to set ownership to `root:ssl-cert` and permissions to `640` for the private key file, typically `/etc/ssl/private/server.key`, using `sudo chown root:ssl-cert` and `sudo chmod 640`.
How do you configure Apache to use a self-signed SSL certificate after it has been created?

You must edit Apache's SSL configuration file (e.g., `/etc/apache2/sites-available/default-ssl.conf`) to point `SSLCertificateFile` and `SSLCertificateKeyFile` to your generated certificate and key files, and also add `SSLCertificateChainFile`.
What measures can be taken to tighten security for an Apache web server using SSL, beyond just enabling the certificate?
You can force all HTTP traffic to HTTPS, require more modern versions of SSL by disabling older protocols (SSLv2, SSLv3), and use stronger cipher options.
What is the purpose of the `ssllabs` ssltest tool mentioned in the document?
The `ssllabs` ssltest tool is used to check the security settings of your web server's SSL configuration and suggest improvements.
What happens if you miss the `-nodes` option when creating a self-signed certificate with the `openssl` command?
If you miss the `-nodes` option, the `openssl` command will likely ask for a pass phrase, which is generally undesirable for automated server operations.
What security measures should be considered when making a cloud-based virtual machine accessible to the public, such as for a web server?

When making a virtual machine publicly accessible, several security measures must be considered. Firstly, you should manage and restrict access to ports using OpenStack's security groups, which allows granting access only to specific IP addresses or ranges. This helps improve VM security. Secondly, it is highly recommended to use encryption, such as Transport Layer Security (TLS), for any data transmission, especially for logins or sensitive information. This prevents eavesdroppers from reading data and third parties from modifying it during transmission. Users are ultimately responsible for the security of their virtual machines and should take these considerations seriously.
What are the initial steps to install and set up an Apache web server on an Ubuntu Linux virtual machine in the cloud?

To install and set up an Apache web server on an Ubuntu Linux virtual machine in the cloud, you must first create a persistent Ubuntu Linux VM. Then, open port 80 to allow HTTP requests into your VM, similar to how you would open SSH access. Once logged into your VM, update your apt-get repositories with `sudo apt-get update`, and upgrade Ubuntu to its latest version with `sudo apt-get upgrade` to ensure you have the latest security patches. Finally, install the Apache web server using the command `sudo apt-get install apache2`. You can verify the installation by navigating to your VM's floating IP address in a web browser, which should display the Apache2 test page.
Why might it be necessary to limit bandwidth on an Apache web server?
Limiting bandwidth on an Apache web server might be necessary if the server is in high demand, as it could otherwise use considerable bandwidth resources.
What are the commands required to install and enable the Apache `mod_bw` bandwidth module?
To install the Apache `mod_bw` bandwidth module, you first run `sudo apt install libapache2-mod-bw`. After installation, you enable the module using the command `sudo a2enmod bw`.
How can you configure the Apache `mod_bw` module to limit all client connections to 100Mbps, and where should this configuration be placed?

To configure the Apache `mod_bw` module to limit all client connections to 100Mbps, you would add the following configuration: `BandWidthModule On`, `ForceBandWidthModule On`, and `BandWidth all 12500000`. This code should be placed between the `<VirtualHost></VirtualHost>` tags for your site, typically in the default Apache site configuration file found at `/etc/apache2/sites-enabled/000-default.conf`.
What are the final steps to complete changing the Apache web server's root directory to a user's home directory?

To complete changing the Apache web server's root directory, you must first create the `public_html` directory in the Ubuntu user's home directory using `mkdir public_html`. Next, copy the default `index.html` page from `/var/www/html` to `/home/ubuntu/public_html` with `cp /var/www/html/index.html /home/ubuntu/public_html`. Finally, restart the Apache server with `sudo service apache2 restart` for the changes to take effect.
What is the primary advantage of changing the Apache web server's root directory to `/home/ubuntu/public_html`?

The primary advantage of changing the Apache web server's root directory to `/home/ubuntu/public_html` is that it allows the user to edit website files, such as `/home/ubuntu/public_html/index.html`, without needing to use the `sudo` command, making content management easier.
What is the main purpose of the "Creating an Apache web server on your cloud VM" page on Alliance clouds?
The page describes how to create a web server on Alliance clouds using Ubuntu Linux and the Apache web server, focusing on the simplest case.
What are the key security considerations when making a computer accessible to the public on Alliance clouds?

Key security considerations include managing and restricting access to ports using OpenStack security groups, encrypting data with Transport Layer Security (TLS) to prevent eavesdropping and modification, and taking responsibility for the security of your virtual machines.
Why is Transport Layer Security (TLS) recommended for web servers on Alliance clouds?
TLS is recommended to encrypt data, such as passwords, sent from or to the web server, which prevents eavesdroppers from reading the information and third parties from modifying data.
What operating system and web server are used in the example for creating a web server on Alliance clouds?
The example uses Ubuntu Linux as the operating system and Apache as the web server.
What are the initial steps required before installing Apache on a cloud VM according to the guide?
Users must first create a persistent Ubuntu Linux virtual machine and open port 80 to allow HTTP requests into the VM.
What commands are used to install the Apache web server after logging into an Ubuntu VM?
After logging into the VM, users should run `sudo apt-get update`, `sudo apt-get upgrade`, and `sudo apt-get install apache2` to install Apache.
How can a user verify that the Apache web server has been successfully installed on their cloud VM?
To verify, a user should enter the VM's floating IP address into a web browser, which should display an Apache2 test page.
Why might a user want to change the default web server's root directory for Apache on their VM?

Changing the default web server's root directory, for example to `/home/ubuntu/public_html`, makes it easier to manage website files as they can be owned by the user connecting to the VM without needing `sudo`.
What configuration files need to be modified to change Apache's web server root directory to `/home/ubuntu/public_html`?
The `apache2.conf` file (specifically the `<Directory /var/www/>` line) and the `000-default.conf` file (specifically the `DocumentRoot /var/www/html` line) need to be modified.
After changing the web server's root directory and copying files, what command should be run to apply these changes?
The command `sudo service apache2 restart` should be run to apply the changes to the Apache server.
Why would someone want to limit the bandwidth of an Apache web server on Alliance clouds?
Limiting bandwidth is useful for Apache web servers in high demand to manage and conserve considerable bandwidth resources.
What Apache module is used to limit overall bandwidth usage?
The `mod_bw` Apache bandwidth module is used to limit overall bandwidth usage.
What commands are used to install and enable the Apache bandwidth module?
To install, use `sudo apt install libapache2-mod-bw`. To enable, use `sudo a2enmod bw`.
Where should the configuration for limiting bandwidth using `mod_bw` be placed in the Apache configuration files?

The `mod_bw` configuration should be placed between the `<VirtualHost></VirtualHost>` tags for your site, typically in the `/etc/apache2/sites-enabled/000-default.conf` file for the default Apache site.
What are some recommended next steps after setting up a basic Apache web server on an Alliance cloud VM?
Recommended next steps include configuring Apache to use SSL, referring to the Apache2 documentation, and exploring HTML tutorials.
What is the upcoming change regarding database server availability on the Graham cluster?
As of January 13, 2025, the Graham cluster will be operating at approximately 25% capacity and will no longer provide a database server during its transition period until Nibi is available.
What types of database servers does the Alliance offer to researchers, and what specialized extension is available on the Cedar PostgreSQL server?

The Alliance provides researchers with access to MySQL and PostgreSQL database servers on the Cedar cluster. The Cedar PostgreSQL server includes a PostGIS extension, which is available for those who need to perform geocoding.
How does a researcher obtain a MySQL account on the Cedar MySQL server, and what information must be included in their request?

To obtain a MySQL account with privileges to create databases on the Cedar MySQL server, a researcher must send a request to Technical Support. The request needs to include their Alliance username and the amount of database space required for their project.
When using the `mysql` client to connect to the MySQL server, what specific options should be avoided, and why?

Users should not use the `-p` or `-h` options as arguments when running `mysql`. The necessary password and server name are automatically taken from the `.my.cnf` file located in the user's home directory.
When is it appropriate to execute SQL commands directly from the head node, and when must a script issuing SQL commands be submitted as a job to the scheduler?

It is acceptable to submit a long-running SQL command from the head node because most of the CPU usage occurs on the database server side. However, if a script issues SQL commands and consumes a lot of CPU, it needs to be submitted as a job to the scheduler.
How do researchers create a new MySQL database on the Cedar cluster, and what naming conventions must they follow?

To create a MySQL database on the Cedar cluster, researchers must use the `CREATE DATABASE` command in the `mysql` client. The database's name is arbitrary but must start with the researcher's MySQL username, followed by an underscore. For example, if the username is 'david', the database name must begin with 'david_'. Researchers can create multiple databases as long as they follow this naming rule, and these databases will be accessible from the Cedar head node, Cedar compute nodes, and Cedar Portal.
How can an Alliance MySQL account holder on the Cedar cluster share a table from their database with another user for specific privileges?

To share a MySQL table on the Cedar cluster, the account holder needs to connect to MySQL, use the specific database, and then issue a `GRANT` command. For example, to grant 'SELECT' (read-only) privileges on 'mytable' within 'david_db' to a user named 'john', the command would be `GRANT SELECT on mytable to 'john'@'172.%';`. The `172.%` specifies the network from which the user can connect.
What information should researchers include when submitting a request for a PostgreSQL account and database on the Cedar cluster?

Researchers requesting a PostgreSQL account and database on the Cedar cluster must send a request to Technical Support. This request needs to include their Alliance username, the amount of database space required for their project, and whether they need the PostGIS extension enabled for their database.
How do researchers access their PostgreSQL accounts on the Cedar server, and what are the security guidelines regarding passwords?

Researchers do not need to supply a password to access their PostgreSQL accounts on the Cedar server. For security, Alliance passwords must never be required or used in scripts, and one user cannot directly access another user's database. Users connect by running the "psql" client, and it's recommended to load the 'postgresql' module for the latest features by running `module load postgresql`.
What are the steps to share data from a PostgreSQL database with another user on the Cedar server?

To share data from a PostgreSQL database on the Cedar server, the person receiving access must first have their own Postgres account. What is the Database as a Service (DBaaS) offering, and how can researchers request access to these cloud-based database servers?

What is the process for determining a user's PostgreSQL account username on the Cedar server?

Can researchers create their own PostgreSQL databases on the Cedar server, or are they assigned?

How can a researcher establish an SSL connection to a PostgreSQL database instance on a Database as a Service (DBaaS) host?

How do researchers connect to the Cedar MySQL server?

What information is required to request a MySQL account on the Cedar cluster?

How can a user share a table from their MySQL database on Cedar with another user?

What is OpenStack, and what are its primary functions on our clouds?

OpenStack is a software suite used on our clouds to control hardware resources such as computers, storage, and networking. Its primary functions include allowing the creation and management of virtual machines (VMs or instances) through software emulation, which provides complete control over the computing environment, and supporting diverse use cases ranging from hosting websites to creating virtual clusters.
What is the OpenStack dashboard, and what is its relationship with Horizon?

The OpenStack dashboard is the web browser user interface used to manage your cloud resources. It is developed under an OpenStack sub-project referred to as Horizon, and the terms "Horizon" and "dashboard" might be used interchangeably.
In OpenStack, what are projects, and how do they manage virtual machines and resources?

OpenStack projects group virtual machines (VMs) together and provide a quota from which VMs and related resources can be created. All accounts that are members of a project have the same level of permissions. Projects are unique to a particular cloud and are typically owned by primary investigators (PIs), who must request new projects, quota adjustments, and confirm access for new members.
What is the purpose of the default security group in OpenStack, and what are its standard pre-configured rules?

The default security group allows a virtual machine (VM) to access the internet for tasks like downloading operating system upgrades or package installations. However, it prevents other machines from accessing the VM, except for other VMs belonging to the same default security group. Its standard rules include two Egress rules (one for IPv4 and one for IPv6) to allow unlimited outbound network access, and two Ingress rules (one for IPv4 and one for IPv6) to permit communication among VMs within that same security group.
What does CIDR stand for, and how are CIDR rules utilized to define IP address ranges when managing security groups?

CIDR stands for Classless Inter-Domain Routing, which is a standardized method for defining IP address ranges. When managing security groups, CIDR rules are used to specify allowed IP addresses or ranges for Ingress rules. A CIDR rule, such as `192.168.1.1/24`, uses a `/XX` suffix to indicate how many of the leftmost bits of an IP address must match. For example, `/24` means the first 24 bits (3 bytes) must match, while `/32` requires an exact match of all 32 bits, and `/0` allows any IP address to match.
How can a user customize an OpenStack virtual machine (VM) when it is launched for the first time, using cloudInit?

A user can customize an OpenStack VM the first time it is launched by using cloudInit. This can be done through two main methods: either by using the OpenStack command-line interface or by pasting a cloudInit script into the 'Customization Script' field available in the OpenStack dashboard, found under the 'Configuration' option when launching an instance (Project --> Compute --> Instances --> Launch instance button).
What is the purpose of a security group for virtual machines?
A security group is a set of rules designed to control network traffic flowing into and out of your virtual machines.
How can users manage security groups within OpenStack?

To manage security groups, navigate to 'Project->Network->Security Groups' in the OpenStack dashboard. Here, you will see a list of currently defined security groups, including a default one if no others have been created.
What are the steps to add or remove rules from an existing security group?

To add or remove rules from a security group, click 'Manage Rules' beside the specific group. Once the group description is displayed, you can utilize the '+Add Rule' and 'Delete Rule' buttons to modify its rules.
What is cloudInit used for in OpenStack?
CloudInit is used to customize a virtual machine (VM) instance the first time it is launched in OpenStack.
How can users apply cloudInit customizations when launching a VM instance in OpenStack?

Users can apply cloudInit customizations either through the OpenStack command-line interface or by pasting their cloudInit script into the "Customization Script" field found under the "Configuration" option on the OpenStack dashboard's "Launch instance" page (Project-->Compute-->Instances).
What is a common use case for cloudInit during VM creation?
A common use case for cloudInit during VM creation is to add multiple users to the virtual machine.
What is the purpose of using cloudInit when creating a virtual machine (VM)?
CloudInit allows for customization of a VM during its creation, such as adding users with specific permissions (e.g., sudo access) and their corresponding SSH public keys.
How do you add multiple users, including preserving the default distribution user, to a new virtual machine using a cloudInit script?

To add multiple users and preserve the default distribution user (like debian, centos, or ubuntu) on a new VM, you would use a YAML-formatted cloudInit script. The script should include `users: - default` followed by each additional user's details, such as their name, shell, sudo permissions, and SSH authorized keys. It's essential that at least one user has sudo permissions, especially if the default user is overwritten.
How can you confirm that public keys have been successfully added for users after a virtual machine has been launched with cloudInit?

After the virtual machine has finished launching, you can verify that the public keys have been correctly added by checking the instance's log. This log is accessible by clicking on the instance's name on the "Compute->Instances" panel and then selecting the "log" tab. The log should display information indicating that the authorized keys were added for the specified users.

How can a new user account be created on an Ubuntu Linux virtual machine (VM) and configured for SSH access?

How does one grant administrative or root user privileges to an existing user on an Ubuntu Linux virtual machine (VM)?

On an Ubuntu Linux VM, administrative or root user privileges can be given to a user by running the command `sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users`. This command opens an editor where a line similar to `USERNAME ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL` should be added.

What is Nextcloud, and what are its primary features for Alliance users?

Nextcloud is a Dropbox-like cloud storage service provided for all Alliance users, accessible at https://nextcloud.computecanada.ca/ using an Alliance username and password. All data transfers between local devices and Alliance's Nextcloud are encrypted. The service offers a fixed quota of 100 GB per user and implements a daily backup policy without offsite copies.
What are the recommended methods for accessing and managing files on the Alliance Nextcloud service?

Users can access and manage files on the Alliance Nextcloud service through a web interface, the Nextcloud Desktop Sync Client, Nextcloud mobile apps, and any WebDAV client. The web interface allows users to upload, download, edit, and share files, while the Desktop Sync Client and mobile apps synchronize data between local devices and Nextcloud automatically.
What is the key difference between using a WebDAV client and a Synchronization client to access Alliance Nextcloud storage?

When using a WebDAV client, your Nextcloud storage is mounted on your computer, meaning files are not copied locally; any edits you make are applied directly to the original file on the Alliance Nextcloud system at Simon Fraser University. In contrast, a Synchronization client first copies and synchronizes your Nextcloud files to your own computer. This allows you to work on files offline, with changes automatically re-copied to all synchronized systems once network connectivity is re-established.
How can a user configure and use `rclone` to upload and download files to Alliance Nextcloud, and what advantage does it offer over `curl`?

`rclone` allows users to create a persistent configuration profile for remote storage devices, eliminating the need to re-enter service details and passwords for repeated use, unlike `curl`. The password is stored encrypted in `~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf`. To use it, first ensure `rclone` is installed (it's available on Alliance clusters). Then, configure a new remote profile by running `rclone config`, choosing 'n' for 'New remote', naming it (e.g., 'nextcloud'), selecting WebDAV as the storage type, providing the URL `https://nextcloud.computecanada.ca/remote.php/dav/files/<your CCDB username>`, your CCDB username, and password. Once configured, files can be uploaded using `rclone copy /path/to/local/file nextcloud:remote/path` and downloaded with `rclone copy nextcloud:remote/path/file .`.
What are the steps to map an Alliance Nextcloud WebDAV drive on a Windows computer?

Alternatively, third-party clients like Cyberduck, which is available for Windows, can also be used.
What is the WebDAV URL used to mount an Alliance Nextcloud folder on a computer, and how can files be managed once it's mounted?

To mount an Alliance Nextcloud folder on your computer using a WebDAV client, use the URL `https://nextcloud.computecanada.ca/remote.php/webdav/`. Once mounted, files can be managed by dragging and dropping them between the WebDAV drive and your local computer.
What are the specific steps for Mac OSX users to mount an Alliance Nextcloud folder using a WebDAV client?

What information is required to configure a new Nextcloud remote device profile using `rclone`?

How do you upload and download files to a Nextcloud remote using the `rclone` command-line tool?

The Nextcloud Desktop Synchronization Client synchronizes files between a local computer and the Nextcloud folder, allowing users to work offline and automatically updates files when network connectivity is re-established.
How do WebDAV clients connect to the Alliance Nextcloud service, and what is the required URL?
WebDAV clients can mount a Nextcloud folder to a computer using the WebDAV URL: `https://nextcloud.computecanada.ca/remote.php/webdav/`, enabling drag-and-drop file transfers.
What is the key difference between using a WebDAV client and a Synchronization client for Alliance Nextcloud?

WebDAV clients mount the Nextcloud storage, allowing direct editing of files on the server, while Synchronization clients copy and synchronize files locally, enabling offline work and ensuring files are the same across all synchronized systems.
Which command-line tools can be used to copy files between a Unix computer and Alliance Nextcloud?
`curl` and `cadaver` are command-line clients available for copying files between a Unix computer and Nextcloud.
What is the command to upload a file to Alliance Nextcloud using `curl`?
To upload a file using `curl`, the command is: `curl -k -u <username> -T <filename> https://nextcloud.computecanada.ca/remote.php/webdav/`.
What is `rclone`, and what benefit does it offer over `curl` for managing files with Alliance Nextcloud?
`rclone` is a command-line utility that allows users to create a configured remote storage profile once, storing credentials encrypted, which streamlines repeated file transfers compared to `curl`.
How can Alliance users share files with other registered Alliance users within Nextcloud?
Users can share files by selecting a file or directory and typing the user's first name, last name, or username, or by using their CCDB group name.
How can an Alliance Nextcloud user share a file with someone who does not have an Alliance account?

Is the `rclone` utility readily available on Alliance clusters, and if so, where is it typically located?

What is the primary function of the OpenStack command line tool?

The OpenStack command line tool allows users to perform many actions available through the OpenStack dashboard GUI, and it also provides some additional functionality that the dashboard does not. It can be utilized from any machine, virtual or otherwise, provided there is an internet connection and the client is installed.
How are the OpenStack command line tools installed on different Linux distributions?

The OpenStack command line tools are Python-based. For Ubuntu, install with `sudo apt-get install python python-dev python-pip` followed by `sudo pip install python-openstackclient`. For CentOS 7, run `yum install epel-release`, then `yum install gcc python python-dev python2-pip`, and finally `pip install python-openstackclient` as root. For Fedora, use `sudo dnf install python-openstackclient`. If administrative privileges are not available, Python and pip must be installed by other means, and then `pip install --user python-openstackclient` can be used.
What is the process for connecting the OpenStack command line client to an OpenStack project?

After downloading, source the file using a command like `source <project name>-openrc.sh`. You will be asked for your OpenStack password, which is your CCDB password. You can test the setup by typing `openstack image list`.
What are some of the command groups available for managing resources using the OpenStack command-line interface?

The OpenStack command-line interface provides several command groups for managing various resources, including `server`, `volume`, `console`, `flavor`, `image`, `ip`, `keypair`, `network`, `snapshot`, `security group`, and `limits`.
What operations can be performed on servers using the `server` command group in the OpenStack command-line interface?

The `server` command group in the OpenStack CLI allows users to perform operations such as adding security groups or volumes, creating, deleting, listing, showing, setting, starting, stopping, rebooting, pausing, resuming, migrating, resizing, rebuilding, shelving, unshelving, locking, unlocking, rescuing, unrescuing servers, creating image dumps, and establishing SSH connections.
How can a user access help for a particular command within the OpenStack command-line interface?
To get help on a particular command (e.g., options and arguments of the command), one can type `help <command group> <command>`.
Are all commands in the OpenStack command-line interface accessible to every user, or are there restrictions?
Many commands are available only to OpenStack administrators and will return an error message if a non-administrator tries using them.
What functionality does the `limits` command group offer in the OpenStack command-line interface?
The `limits` command group provides the ability to `show` resource limits within the OpenStack command-line interface.
Which commands are available for managing security groups and their rules through the OpenStack CLI?
For security groups, you can `create`, `delete`, `list`, `set`, and `show` them. For security group rules, you can `create`, `delete`, `list`, and `show` them.
What separate command-line interfaces are available for OpenStack, beyond the main `openstack` command?

Is additional installation required to use the separate OpenStack command-line tools like `nova` or `glance`?
No, additional installation is not required for these separate OpenStack command-line tools. They are installed simultaneously with the main `openstack` command.
What OpenStack component is managed using the `heat` command-line interface?
The `heat` command-line interface is specifically used for working with orchestration in OpenStack.
What is the primary purpose of the OpenStack command-line tool, and what are its key advantages over the OpenStack dashboard GUI?

The OpenStack command-line tool allows users to perform many actions available through the OpenStack dashboard GUI, while also providing some unique functionalities not found in the dashboard. It can be used from any machine with an internet connection and the client installed.

What is the recommended installation method for the OpenStack command-line tools if a user does not have administrative privileges on their Linux machine?

How do users configure their environment to connect the OpenStack command-line client to their OpenStack project?

What specific modification is required for the OpenStack RC file when connecting to the new Arbutus cloud?

What should a user be cautious about when switching between different OpenStack RC files?

What are the two main ways to execute commands using the OpenStack command-line tool?

Commands can be executed interactively by typing `openstack` and then issuing commands at the prompt, or as one-off commands by preceding the command with `openstack`, such as `openstack server list`.
How can users access help information for command groups and specific commands within the OpenStack command-line interface?

Users can type `help` at the OpenStack prompt to see available command groups, `help <command group>` to list commands within a specific group, and `help <command group> <command>` to get details like options and arguments for a particular command.
Which OpenStack command group is primarily used for managing virtual machine instances, and what are some common actions it supports?
The `server` command group is used for managing virtual machine instances, supporting actions such as `create`, `delete`, `start`, `stop`, `reboot`, `suspend`, `pause`, `resize`, and `list`.
What types of operations can users perform using the `image` command group in the OpenStack CLI?
The `image` command group allows users to `create`, `delete`, `list`, `save`, `set`, and `show` images within their OpenStack project.
What capabilities does the `security group` command group offer for managing network access in OpenStack?
The `security group` command group allows users to `create`, `delete`, `list`, `set`, and `show` security groups, as well as `create`, `delete`, `list`, and `show` rules within those security groups.

What actions does the Alliance support team take when they detect a compromised virtual machine (VM)?

Our support team confirms the compromise by investigating network traffic logs and other sources. Following confirmation, the VM is shut down and locked at the sysadmin level, and you are notified by email.
Why is it necessary to build a new virtual machine (VM) after an existing one has been compromised?

It is necessary to build a new VM because you cannot start an administratively locked VM. Additionally, while it is relatively safe to extract data, the contents of the compromised VM are no longer trustworthy, compelling you to build a new one.
What is the first step a user should take when initiating a data recovery plan for a compromised virtual machine (VM)?
The first step is to send an email to cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca outlining your recovery plan. If access to the filesystem is required for recovery, the cloud support team will then unlock the volume.
What is the main purpose of the Alliance Cloud document regarding compromised Virtual Machines (VMs)?
The document sets out what you need to do to recover data out of a VM that has been compromised on the Alliance Cloud.
Who holds the primary responsibility for recovering data from a compromised VM on the Alliance Cloud?
You, the user, are responsible for recovering data out of a VM that has been compromised.
What are the first three steps taken by the support team when a compromised VM is detected on the Alliance Cloud?
The support team confirms the compromise by investigating network traffic logs, shuts down and locks the VM at the sysadmin level, and notifies you by email.
Why is it necessary to rebuild a new VM after an existing one is compromised on the Alliance Cloud?
You cannot start an administratively locked VM, its contents are no longer trustworthy, and a new VM has to be built.
What is the initial action a user should take after their VM is detected as compromised on the Alliance Cloud?
Send an email to cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca outlining your recovery plan, especially if access to the filesystem is required.
Which console should a user log into to begin data rescue operations for a compromised VM on the Alliance Cloud?
Users should log in to the OpenStack admin console.
What type of new instance should be launched within OpenStack for data recovery from a compromised VM on the Alliance Cloud?
Launch a new instance that will be used for data rescue operations.
How does a user detach the compromised volume from its original VM in the OpenStack admin console on the Alliance Cloud?
Under 'Volumes', select 'Manage Attachments' from the dropdown list for the compromised volume and click on the 'Detach Volume' button.
To which instance should the compromised volume be attached for data rescue operations on the Alliance Cloud?
The compromised volume should be attached to the recovery instance that was just launched.
Once a user SSHes into their recovery instance, how will the old, compromised volume appear on the Alliance Cloud?
The old, compromised volume will be available as the 'vdb' disk.
What guidance is provided for mounting the appropriate filesystem from a compromised volume on the Alliance Cloud?
Because instructions vary greatly depending on how the base OS image was created, contact someone with experience to continue.
Is it considered safe to extract data from a compromised VM on the Alliance Cloud?
Yes, while the contents of the VM are no longer trustworthy, it is relatively safe to extract the data.
What email address should be used to contact cloud support regarding a recovery plan for a compromised VM on the Alliance Cloud?
The email address is cloud@tech.alliancecan.ca.
What happens to the compromised VM's volume if filesystem access is needed for recovery on the Alliance Cloud?
If access to the filesystem is required, the cloud support team will unlock the volume.
What is the primary responsibility of a user when running virtual machines on the cloud?
On the cloud, users are solely responsible for the security of their virtual machines.
What are the recommended practices for keeping a virtual machine's operating system secured on the cloud?

To keep a VM's operating system secure, users should apply security updates regularly, avoid using packages from unknown sources, use a recent operating system image, utilize SSH key authentication instead of passwords (as it's more secure), and install fail2ban to block brute-force attacks.
Which specific services and ports should generally not be made publicly accessible when configuring network security for a virtual machine?

When configuring network security, services that should generally not be made publicly accessible include ssh (port 22), RDP (port 3389), mysql (port 3306), VNC (ports 5900-5906), postgresql (port 5432), nosql, and tomcat. Users should also avoid running mail or BitTorrent servers and limit access by not using '0.0.0.0' in CIDR fields for security groups.
Who is primarily responsible for the security of virtual machines created on the CC-Cloud?
Users are responsible for the security of their virtual machines on the cloud.
What is the main objective of the document outlining security considerations for virtual machines on the cloud?
The document aims to set out key considerations for users regarding security when creating a VM on the cloud, rather than being a complete guide.
Is there a supplementary video resource available for understanding basic security considerations for VMs in the cloud?
Yes, there is an approximately 1.5-hour recording on YouTube titled 'Safety First!' that covers basic security considerations when working with VMs in the cloud.
How often should security updates be applied to a virtual machine's operating system to maintain its security?
Security updates should be applied on a regular basis, ideally weekly, or as often as new packages become available.
When creating a new virtual machine, what type of operating system image is recommended for better security?
It is recommended to use a recent operating system image; for example, Ubuntu 18.04 instead of Ubuntu 14.04.
What is the preferred authentication method for cloud instances, and why is it more secure than password-based authentication?
SSH key authentication is used by default and is preferred because enabling password-based authentication is significantly less secure.
What tool is recommended to block brute-force attacks on a virtual machine?
Installing fail2ban is recommended to block brute-force attacks on a VM.
What specific CIDR configuration should be avoided when defining network access rules in a security group for a virtual machine?
It is advised to avoid using '0.0.0.0' in the CIDR field of the security group form, especially in the default security group.
What caution should be exercised regarding port ranges when configuring network security rules for a virtual machine?
It is advised not to bundle ranges of ports when allowing access.
Which common services are explicitly listed as services that should NOT be made publicly accessible from the internet on a virtual machine?
Services like SSH (22), RDP (3389), MySQL (3306), VNC (5900-5906), and PostgreSQL (5432) should not be made publicly accessible.
What are examples of services that are generally intended to be publicly accessible from the internet on a virtual machine?
Apache (80, 443) and Nginx (80, 443) are examples of services meant to be publicly accessible.
How should web servers be configured for security on a virtual machine, specifically regarding HTTP and HTTPS usage?
Web servers should be configured to use HTTPS instead of HTTP, and in many cases, HTTP should only be used to redirect traffic to HTTPS.
For security reasons, which two types of servers are explicitly advised against running on a virtual machine?
It is advised not to run a mail server or a BitTorrent server on a virtual machine.
What is the general procedure for updating a Linux virtual machine's operating system to keep it secure?
The general procedure involves running specific update commands for the distribution, followed by a reboot, and then reconnecting to the VM.
What are the recommended commands to update and reboot an Ubuntu/Debian Linux virtual machine?
The recommended commands are `$ sudo apt-get update`, `$ sudo apt-get dist-upgrade`, and `$ sudo reboot`.
What commands should be used to update and reboot a CentOS Linux virtual machine?
The commands to update and reboot a CentOS Linux VM are `$ sudo yum update` and `$ sudo reboot`.
What commands are used to update and reboot a Fedora Linux virtual machine?
The commands to update and reboot a Fedora Linux VM are `$ sudo dnf update` and `$ sudo reboot`.
At what point in the 'Safety First!' YouTube recording can one find information specifically about OpenStack security groups?
Information about OpenStack security groups can be found starting at the 1530-second mark of the 'Safety First!' recording.
How can HTTP TRACE and TRACK methods be disabled in Apache on a virtual machine?

To disable HTTP TRACE and TRACK methods in Apache, you need to add the line `TraceEnable off` to an Apache configuration file, such as `/etc/httpd/conf.d/custom.conf`, and then restart the `httpd` service.
What is a simple solution for resolving common SSL certificate issues, such as expiry, untrusted certificates, or self-signed certificates, on a VM running Apache?

If you manage your own domain name for your VM, a simple solution for SSL certificate issues (like expiry, untrusted, self-signed, or missing HSTS) is to remove the entire default configuration section for `<VirtualHost _default_:443>` from your `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf` file, and then restart the `httpd` service.
What is the primary purpose of this document concerning virtual machines in cloud services?
This document provides suggested solutions to common security issues detected on virtual machines running in cloud services.
Who is likely to receive communications from the security team regarding detected issues on virtual machines?
Individuals responsible for one or more virtual machines running in the cloud services are likely to receive such communications.
What is a common security issue related to HTTP methods that can be detected on virtual machines?
A common security issue is when HTTP TRACE / TRACK methods are allowed on virtual machines.
How can the HTTP TRACE / TRACK methods be disabled in Apache?
They can be disabled by adding the line `TraceEnable off` to an Apache configuration file and then restarting the `httpd` service.
Which Apache configuration file is suggested for adding the `TraceEnable off` line?
A configuration file such as `/etc/httpd/conf.d/custom.conf` is suggested for adding the `TraceEnable off` line.
What service must be restarted after modifying an Apache configuration file to disable HTTP TRACE / TRACK methods?
The `httpd` service must be restarted after modifying an Apache configuration file to disable HTTP TRACE / TRACK methods.
What are some common SSL certificate-related issues that might be detected on HTTPS servers?
Common issues include SSL Certificate Expiry, SSL Certificate Cannot Be Trusted, SSL Self-Signed Certificate, and HSTS Missing From HTTPS Server.
What often causes SSL certificate errors like 'Cannot Be Trusted' or 'Self-Signed' for VMs where the user manages their own domain?
These errors may be caused by Apache's default configuration, which serves a self-signed certificate installed with Apache.
What section should be removed from the `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf` file to resolve SSL certificate issues caused by Apache's default configuration?
The entire `<VirtualHost _default_:443> ... </VirtualHost>` section should be removed from the `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf` file.
What is the purpose of removing the default VirtualHost section from Apache's SSL configuration?
Removing this section tells Apache to not reply to requests other than your configured virtual hosts, which helps resolve SSL certificate issues.
After removing the default VirtualHost section from `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf`, what is the necessary next step?
The `httpd` service must be restarted after removing the default VirtualHost section from `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf`.
Which Apache configuration file is associated with resolving SSL certificate issues by removing a default VirtualHost section?
The `/etc/httpd/conf.d/ssl.conf` file is associated with resolving SSL certificate issues by removing a default VirtualHost section.
Why is VNC recommended over SSH + X11 forwarding for accessing graphical user interfaces on a virtual machine?
VNC is recommended for accessing graphical user interfaces (GUIs) on a virtual machine (VM) because it typically provides better performance compared to using SSH with X11 forwarding.
What are the initial steps for setting up a remote desktop with VNC on a virtual machine running the Ubuntu operating system?

What are the specific commands used to install the MATE desktop environment and the TigerVNC server on a Ubuntu virtual machine?

Why is it recommended to close port 5901 after connecting to a VNC server via an SSH tunnel?
Once connected to a VNC server through an SSH tunnel, port 5901 is no longer required to be open. It is recommended to remove this rule from your security groups for improved security.
What command is used to stop a VNC server on a virtual machine?

What are the initial steps required to set up a VNC remote desktop on a Ubuntu virtual machine?

How can a user establish a secure connection to a VNC server running on their virtual machine, and what action is recommended afterwards?

What is the main purpose of setting up a remote desktop with VNC on a virtual machine (VM) running Ubuntu?
The main purpose is to allow users to access graphical user interfaces (GUIs) on their VM with potentially better performance than using SSH + X11 forwarding.
